articles.title: I bought land on Facebook Marketplace for $40K. Now I live there with a single mom I met on Threads and our 3 kids.
articles.summary: After meeting another single mom on Threads, Yolanda Williams invited her to live on her Arkansas land. They now share parenting duties.
articles.body:
Yolanda Williams, 46, bought 3 acres in Arkansas and moved there with her daughter.

She invited another single mom she met online to live on the property with her two kids.

They now share expenses, childcare, and emotional support in what they call a "mommune."

This as-told-to essay is based on a conversation with Yolanda Williams, 46, who lives in central Arkansas with her 9-year-old daughter on a farm with another single mom and her two kids. They help each other with childcare, mental support, and more. This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

In 2021, after my daughter Gia and I got COVID, we decided to take a drive one day. I came across this one little road that I fell in love with.

We kept coming back, driving around this neighborhood in Arkansas , and it became our Sunday thing. We'd get in the car and get ourselves a sweet treat — me a coffee and her a cinnamon roll — and drive around for an hour looking at all the different farms and houses and really just visualizing the life we wanted.

We did that for two years before I found our 3.19-acre land in rural Arkansas. After visiting it, I purchased the land in 2023 on Facebook Marketplace , For-Sale-By-Owner. It cost $40,000 to buy, and I put down $12,000.

It was fully forested raw land, so I could only see part of it, but I used a real estate agent for the process. At the end of 2024, I secured a grant to help pay for the infrastructure, and I spent 2025 getting the land ready to move into. We didn't move until March 2026 because the land needed clearing and practical things such as a driveway and utilities.

The process was expensive because I didn't have much money left to build anything on the land. We got an RV as a place to stay, stash money, and build in the next five years.

Before I'm 50, I would like to have a permanent home built on the land

I'm from Southern California , and when I left in 2017, I was paying $600 to rent a guest room from my friend. Now, I pay $485 for my land mortgage and $400 for my RV payment a month. So, all in all, for me to be on this land, it's around $885 per month. Utilities run about $150 to $200 a month in the summer, and then $100 for water. It's exponentially cheaper to live like this, especially in Arkansas.

Here we have the freedom to roam and to be outside. I'm always in the garden. I've actually lost 30lbs since March because I move so much, and I didn't even realize it. I'm getting a lot more sun and exercise — so is my daughter. I feel more content, I feel more at peace.

However, this move has turned into so much more than that for us. I've been a single mom since my daughter Gia was born. She's 9 now, and I've never truly felt what it's like to have support, to have someone around all the time. By chance, that all changed this year.

I'm not sure who followed who first, but I met a single mom called Sunnie on Threads

She posted on the social media app Threads about wanting to buy land, and I commented back that she should consider Arkansas. I explained to her that land is cheap out here, and I gave her a bunch of information.

A few months later, I randomly saw her posting on Threads that she was in Arkansas with her two kids, who were 11 and 5 years old, looking for land, so I slipped into her DMs, and we exchanged numbers. I texted her to arrange a meet-up and to show her my land. Mind you, this was before I had actually moved onto the property.

The first time we met, we had pizza with the kids. They had a look around, and the kids played really well together. Gia likes the pizza crust but not the actual pizza, and one of Sunnie's kids likes the pizza but not the crust, so it worked out perfectly.

They helped me around the property as I was in the main stretch of getting everything ready for me to move on to. That's when we got to talking about her potentially living here while she searched for her own land.

Sunnie lived in a different city about an hour from me, and she didn't know anyone in Arkansas. I offered her the chance to stay with us to avoid spending money on hotels and Ubers. Although she wanted to buy her own land, I made it clear that she was welcome to stay with me as long as she wanted to. We now split the mortgage and utility costs in half.

Although we didn't know each other for long, I felt a strong connection and vibe

I loved that she was very much like, "I want to put my gloves on, and I want to help you," when it came to laying the foundations around the property, such as weeding, spraying for ticks, building planters, and sowing seeds. Now we garden together and grow as much as we can — like comfrey, lemon balm, mint, and basil. We even make our own fertilizer.

And you know, that's what's missing. A lot of people want this life, but they don't want to actually roll their sleeves up and get dirty to help one another.

Sunnie was essentially a complete stranger. But what I've been trying to do is listen to myself and trust myself. I really felt a great vibe from Sunnie, and my daughter really took to her. We got along, and it just felt right.

Yes, it's hard to build trust because you can't really trust anyone until you start to be around them all the time, but the whole thing with Sunnie is she came, and we sat, and we had a discussion about money and about expectations and about childcare. You just have to be willing to have the hard conversations in order to build a community, and I want to be around people who understand me.

We're now growing food together and raising wildlings.

What I always try to tell people is we need to decenter and deprioritize romantic relationships and just focus on relationships in general, whatever that support looks like.

Whether that's friendship or family, focus on building that community, and we will get the support we're looking for, but if you're only focused on needing a man or a husband or partner to have security to feel supported, then a lot of people will miss out on invaluable support with friends or other women.

For example, I was having a really hard time this Mother's Day — it's just a hard day for me. Sunnie saw that I wasn't in a good space, so she took the kids and left so I could get some alone time. Having that support and knowing that I can say "hey, I'm having a hard time with motherhood right now" and someone will not only understand but will help me through that by watching my kid for me, taking her to the park, or giving me some space — it has been life-changing. It's the support that I need.

We really just help each other out. When I have to leave and go somewhere, I'll ask her to come inside the RV or to watch Gia play outside, and she does. Vice versa — if she needs me to watch her children, it's really not a big deal. We just ask each other for favors like: "If you're out at the store, can you get me this?"

We communicate really well with each other, and we help each other out any way we need to, and that includes having dinner together sometimes, watching TV together, and I will let her kids come over here so she can have a break and be able to be in her RV by herself, or we'll go to the park so she can be by herself sometimes.

Ever since I met Sunnie, I can just tell there's a change in my nervous system. Having someone here means I can tap out. I'm 46 this year, and I wouldn't trade this mommune we've built for the world.

articles.title: França investiga ataque com coquetel molotov contra policiais | G1
articles.standfirst: Artefato incendiário foi lançado contra agentes durante protestos contra o aumento do custo de vida em Paris; ministro do Interior chamou episódio de "tentativa de assassinato".
articles.summary: Artefato incendiário foi lançado contra agentes durante protestos contra o aumento do custo de vida em Paris; ministro do Interior chamou episódio de "tentativa de assassinato".
articles.body:
O Ministério Público de Paris abriu, neste domingo (1º), uma investigação por tentativa de homicídio após o lançamento de um coquetel molotov contra agentes das forças de segurança durante uma manifestação realizada na capital francesa no último sábado (31). As informações são da AFP.

O ministro do Interior, Laurent Nuñez, classificou o ataque, que deixou ao menos um agente ferido, como uma "tentativa de assassinato".

Segundo o Ministério do Interior, 320 mil pessoas participaram dos atos em toda a França, incluindo 70 mil em Paris. Os organizadores estimaram uma adesão maior, de quase 500 mil manifestantes no país.

Esse foi o terceiro sábado consecutivo de protestos contra o aumento do custo de vida no país. As manifestações foram marcadas por episódios de violência em algumas cidades, incluindo Paris.

Imagens mostram um artefato incendiário artesanal explodindo aos pés de um integrante das forças de segurança no leste de Paris. O agente sofreu ferimentos leves.

Policial é atingido por coquetel molotov durante protestos na França. — Foto: Sameer Al-Doumy/AFP

"Foram lançados artefatos explosivos contra cerca de 15 gendarmes e também contra policiais", detalhou o Ministério Público.

O gendarme atingido pelo coquetel molotov relatou a emissoras de televisão a sensação de queimadura provocada pela explosão. Ele também descreveu uma "chuva" de projéteis lançados contra sua unidade por um grupo que classificou como "determinado".

🔎 Os gendarmes integram uma força de segurança de natureza militar que exerce funções policiais na França.

Ao todo, 779 pessoas foram detidas ao longo do sábado, segundo o Ministério do Interior francês.

articles.title: Protesto por moradia tem confronto com a polícia em Portugal | G1
articles.standfirst: Movimento critica o governo de centro-direita, que pretende facilitar despejos e acabar com os limites para os valores de novos contratos de aluguel.
articles.summary: Movimento critica o governo de centro-direita, que pretende facilitar despejos e acabar com os limites para os valores de novos contratos de aluguel.
articles.body:
Policial coberto em tinta durante manifestação que denuncia a crise habitacional em Portugal. — Foto: Filipe Amorim/AFP

A polícia de choque portuguesa retirou, na madrugada deste domingo (1), dezenas de barracas montadas por manifestantes que protestavam contra a crise de moradia no país. Houve confrontos, uso de cassetetes e 13 prisões em Lisboa e em Porto.

Em Lisboa , dezenas de policiais, alguns acompanhados por cães, desmontaram um acampamento na Praça do Rossio. Em Porto, a operação ocorreu na Praça Dom João Primeiro. As ações começaram por volta das quatro e meia da manhã.

Enquanto os policiais avançavam, os manifestantes gritavam: “Isso está cheirando a ditadura” e “Somos pacíficos”.

Segundo a polícia, seis pessoas foram presas em Lisboa e sete em Porto por não obedecerem às ordens para deixar os locais.

A polícia afirma que manifestantes atiraram garrafas, tinta e artefatos pirotécnicos contra os agentes. Treze policiais ficaram feridos e oito precisaram ser levados ao hospital. Três policiais à paisana também teriam sido agredidos no Porto.

Os manifestantes afirmam que o número de feridos é maior. O grupo Acampada Lisboa diz que mais de 30 pessoas ficaram feridas, dez delas com necessidade de atendimento hospitalar.

Os acampamentos foram montados depois de manifestações pacíficas contra o aumento dos preços dos imóveis e dos aluguéis.

O movimento critica o governo de centro-direita, que pretende facilitar despejos e acabar com os limites para os valores de novos contratos de aluguel. Os manifestantes temem que as mudanças aumentem ainda mais o custo da moradia e deixem os inquilinos mais vulneráveis.

O movimento português segue o exemplo da Espanha, onde manifestantes mantêm acampamentos há semanas em Madri e outras cidades.

articles.title: Incêndio atinge sucata na Zona Norte de Natal | G1
articles.standfirst: Fogo começou na tarde deste domingo (1º), próximo ao Partage Norte Shopping. Corpo de Bombeiros mobilizou três veículos para combater as chamas. Não houve registro de feridos.
articles.summary: Incêndio na Zona Norte de Natal atinge sucata de pneus perto do Partage Shopping; bombeiros foram acionados para conter as chamas e não há registro de feridos.
articles.body:
Um incêndio atingiu uma sucata na tarde deste domingo (1º), na avenida João Medeiros Filho, na Zona Norte de Natal , nas proximidades do Partage Norte Shopping. As chamas provocaram uma grande coluna de fumaça preta, que podia ser vista de diferentes pontos da região.

De acordo com o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Rio Grande do Norte (CBMRN), o fogo atingiu uma área onde havia materiais combustíveis, principalmente pneus. As causas serão investigadas e não houve registro de vítimas.

Apesar de controlado, até às 16h20, os bombeiros ainda tentavam apagar completamente os focos do incêndio. A corporação informou que não havia risco das chamas se espalharem para outras áreas.

Três veículos foram enviados ao local: um caminhão de combate a incêndio, uma unidade de resgate e um carro de apoio.

Fumaça preta chamou atenção de quem passava pela região — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

articles.title: Emicida faz show gratuito no Dia da Consciência Negra em Porto Alegre | G1
articles.standfirst: Artista se apresenta no Dia da Consciência Negra na capital gaúcha, durante a 3ª edição do Encontro Black realizada pelo museu, que terá exposição sobre o Racionais MCs.
articles.summary: Artista se apresenta no Dia da Consciência Negra na capital gaúcha, durante a 3ª edição do Encontro Black realizada pelo museu, que terá exposição sobre o Racionais MCs.
articles.body:
Terceiro lote disponibiliza mil ingressos gratuitos para show de Emicida — Foto: Walter Firmo/Cecropia

No Dia da Consciência Negra, celebrado no Brasil em 20 de novembro, o músico Emicida fará um show gratuito em Porto Alegre . Ele se apresenta ao lado do artista DJ Nyack no Museu da Cultura Hop Hop , que fica na Zona Norte da capital gaúcha.

A apresentação ocorre durante o evento Encontro Black, que também marca a pré-abertura da exposição “Racionais MCs: O Quinto Elemento” .

A programação do evento ainda conta com sets das DJs Vânia e Vanessa e do DJ Luka Groove Chic, além de pocket shows de rap de Lady Dee, Mano Rick, Família Preto Bom, com apresentações de breaking do Coletivo Artistico Gauchóques e Rayo ZC75 e grafite ao vivo de Sol e Triafu.

O line-up também conta com um show de rap do grupo Atitude Feminina e set do DJ Claudio Raffaello Santoro. (Confira a programação completa abaixo)

Fomentado pela Lei Federal de Incentivo à Cultura, com patrocínio master da Petrobras e patrocínios da Caixa Econômica Federal e da Open Society Foundations e realização do Ministério da Cultura e do Governo Federal, o Encontro Black é o evento anual de celebração da Consciência Negra, organizado pelo museu.

Em 2024, Tony Tornado foi a atração principal. Já no último ano, BK´ subiu ao palco. Agora, em 2026, Emicida e DJ Nyack reúnem música, memória e valorização da cultura negra em uma programação especial.

A entrada é gratuita para participar do Encontro Black. Os interessados devem retirar seus ingressos através das redes sociais do museu e da plataforma Sympla. O terceiro lote, com mais mil ingressos, será liberado no dia 09 de novembro, às 20h . Os dois lote iniciais esgotaram em apenas 30 minutos cada , nos dias 20 e 27 de outubro.

Com curadoria de Eliane Dias, “Racionais MC's: O Quinto Elemento” celebra os 38 anos de carreira de um dos maiores grupos de rap do Brasil . O acervo reúne objetos pessoais, figurinos icônicos, fotografias raras e manuscritos originais de composições que atravessaram gerações e ajudaram a consolidar o rap como uma das principais expressões culturais do país.

“Esse é um projeto elaborado com a proposta de mostrar a cultura do rap e do hip hop em lugares inesperados. Espero que as pessoas compareçam, curtam a experiência, que gostem e que entendam a importância de ver a cultura de outras formas para além do cinema, de festas e shows. Que compreendam que exposições e museus são para o nosso povo preto periférico”, afirma a curadora Eliane Dias.

Apresentada anteriormente apenas no Museu das Favelas, em São Paulo, a mostra chega agora a Porto Alegre, que será a segunda cidade brasileira a recebê-la. Após a pré-abertura, em 20 de novembro, a inauguração oficial acontece no dia 26 de novembro de 2026 ficando em cartaz até 26 de novembro de 2027 no segundo andar do Museu da Cultura Hip Hop.

“É com muita alegria que anunciamos a chegada da exposição dos Racionais MCs a Porto Alegre. A importância do grupo para a expansão do hip hop em todo o país e no mundo é inquestionável. Então, ser o segundo local a receber essa exposição, nos deixa imensamente honrados”, comemora Rafa Rafuagi, fundador do Museu da Cultura Hip Hop RS.

Encontro Black 2026 — 20 de novembro (sexta-feira), das 14h às 21h, no Museu da Cultura Hip Hop RS – Rua Parque dos Nativos, 545, Vila Ipiranga, Zona Norte, Porto Alegre (RS).

No Dia da Consciência Negra, o Museu da Cultura Hip Hop realiza a 3ª edição do Encontro Black. São uma tarde e uma noite de shows, DJs, breaking e grafite ao vivo, com food trucks, feira empreendedora e espaço kids, celebrando resistência, criatividade e coletividade.

Pocket shows: Mano Rick, Família Preto Bom e Laddy Dee

DJ sets: DJs Vânia e Vanessa, DJ Luka e DJ R&R

14h30 – Abertura oficial do Encontro Black

15h – Abertura da exposição “O Quinto Elemento” – Racionais MC’s

16h20 – Inauguração do Mirante Petrobras

Inaugurado no ano do cinquentenário do hip hop no mundo, o Museu da Cultura Hip Hop é o primeiro da América Latina dedicado ao movimento. Com um espaço de quatro mil metros quadrados, é uma iniciativa coletiva da Associação da Cultura Hip Hop de Esteio, e objetiva o fortalecimento de outros estados brasileiros para criação de museus, organizando uma rede capaz de construir o Museu Brasileiro da Cultura Hip Hop nos próximos cinco anos.

O complexo conta com cerca de seis mil itens de acervo físico e digital sobre a história do hip hop gaúcho. Inspirado no The Universal Hip Hop Museum nos Estados Unidos, conta com salas expositivas, atelier de oficinas, café, loja, estufa agroecológica, biblioteca, estúdio musical, multipalco e a Quadra Petrobras.

O Museu da Cultura Hip Hop tem financiamento da Lei Federal de Incentivo à Cultura, patrocínio master da Petrobras, patrocínio da Caixa Econômica Federal e da Open Society Foundations. Realização do Ministério da Cultura e do Governo do Brasil.

articles.title: Furto de iPhones em Registro: Ladrão invade loja pelo telhado | G1
articles.standfirst: Um dos suspeitos invadiu o estabelecimento pelo telhado, em Registro (SP). A dupla levou cerca de 24 celulares da Apple, além de aparelhos de outras marcas.
articles.summary: Câmeras flagraram o furto de iPhones em Registro, onde a dupla quebrou o telhado e usou um balde para levar aparelhos avaliados em mais de R$ 83 mil.
articles.body:
Um homem invadiu uma loja de celulares pelo telhado e furtou 24 iPhones em Registro , no interior de São Paulo. Segundo o boletim de ocorrência obtido pelo g1 , 22 dos aparelhos foram avaliados em R$ 83,6 mil.

O crime aconteceu em um estabelecimento localizado na Rua Meraldo Previdi, no Centro da cidade, na segunda-feira (26). De acordo com o registro policial, os suspeitos quebraram uma telha e abriram um buraco no forro de gesso para entrar na loja.

Imagens de segurança mostram um homem de blusa vermelha recolhendo os aparelhos dentro da loja, enquanto outro suspeito aguardava do lado de fora. Nas gravações, o homem aparece colocando os celulares em um balde e passando os aparelhos ao comparsa por uma abertura no telhado.

Homem furtaram mais de 24 celulares em loja de Registro, SP. — Foto: Reprodução/Câmera de Monitoramento

Outra câmera registrou os dois suspeitos fugindo após o furto. O prejuízo total ainda não foi contabilizado, já que outros celulares de marcas diversas também foram levados. A perícia foi acionada.

A Secretaria de Segurança Pública de São Paulo (SSP-SP) informou que o caso foi registrado no 1º Distrito Policial de Registro.

articles.title: Alunos de outros estados escolhem Fortaleza para fazer prova da Fuvest | G1
articles.standfirst: Além de moradores do Ceará, pessoas de outros 22 estados e do Distrito Federal escolheram a capital cearense para realizar as provas. Primeira fase é aplicada neste domingo.
articles.summary: Além de moradores do Ceará, pessoas de outros 22 estados e do Distrito Federal escolheram a capital cearense para realizar as provas.
articles.body:
Pela primeira vez, a Fundação Universitária para o Vestibular (Fuvest) aplica neste domingo (1º) as provas do vestibular da Universidade de São Paulo (USP) em Fortaleza . Ao todo, 1.640 pessoas se inscreveram na capital cearense. Entre os candidatos, há estudantes de outras regiões do Brasil, como Pernambuco, Rio Grande do Norte e Bahia.

Segundo os inscritos, a escolha por Fortaleza ocorreu principalmente por causa da logística: a viagem é menos cansativa e mais barata, o que pode refletir no desempenho na prova. Ter mais tempo para descansar e ficar perto da família também foram pontos citados pelos candidatos.

➡️ A equipe da TV Verdes Mares esteve, na manhã deste domingo, no Centro Universitário 7 de Setembro , o único local de prova em Fortaleza, para acompanhar a movimentação antes do início do certame. Os estudantes se reuniram no portão e entraram no local sem dificuldades. Informações sobre salas e orientações gerais foram colocadas na entrada para facilitar a organização.

Estudantes escolhem Fortaleza para fazer prova da Fuvest e explicam decisão. — Foto: Thiago Gadelha (SVM).

Candidatos de 22 estados e do DF escolheram Fortaleza

O vestibular oferece 8.147 vagas em cursos de graduação. Nesta edição, Fortaleza é a única cidade fora do estado de São Paulo a aplicar as provas.

A decisão gerou elogios nas redes sociais , mas também críticas, principalmente de pessoas que alegam que “cearenses vão roubar as vagas de paulistas”.

No entanto, estudantes afirmam que optar por Fortaleza foi mais vantajoso. Segundo a Fuvest, além de moradores do Ceará, candidatos de outros 22 estados e do Distrito Federal escolheram a capital cearense para fazer a prova.

Kaique de Oliveira Vasconcelos, 18 anos. — Foto: Thiago Gadelha/SVM

É o caso de Kaique de Oliveira Vasconcelos , de 18 anos. O jovem está no 3º ano do ensino médio e faz pela primeira vez o exame da Fuvest. Kaique nasceu em São Paulo, mas mora atualmente em Natal, no Rio Grande do Norte. Ele veio a Fortaleza com o sonho de cursar engenharia química.

“Comecei a estudar desde o ano passado. Estudei várias tardes e noites, todos os dias, de segunda a sábado. Fazia simulados, provas, questões. [Escolhi Fortaleza] por causa da logística. É um pouco mais barato em relação aos preços e também para ficar perto da família. Acho que vai ter um impacto grande no desempenho, em questão de poder descansar mais, na logística do tempo”, disse Kaique.

Goeldi Tenório, 20 anos. — Foto: Thiago Gadelha/Sistema Verdes Mares

Em Recife, capital de Pernambuco, Goeldi Tenório, de 20 anos, se prepara há três anos para tentar uma vaga em medicina. O jovem afirma ter focado, especialmente, na resolução de questões e simulados. Ele também pretende fazer o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem), que ocorre nos dias 8 e 15 de novembro.

Goeldi se preparava para fazer a prova em São Paulo, mas, quando soube que o exame seria realizado em Fortaleza, decidiu mudar os planos:

“A logística foi muito mais fácil, porque aqui em Fortaleza é tudo mais tranquilo, trânsito mais tranquilo, passagem mais barata. Tenho familiares aqui por perto, o que facilita mais (...) O objetivo é chegar na segunda fase. Estou bastante confiante, me preparei bem”, comentou.

O conteúdo desta primeira etapa do vestibular inclui questões de arte, biologia, educação física, filosofia, física, geografia, história, inglês, matemática, português, química e sociologia.

A partir deste ano, a primeira fase tem novidades: serão 80 questões de múltipla escolha. Antes, esta etapa contava com 90 perguntas. O tempo de prova, no entanto, permanece o mesmo: cinco horas.

Maria Eduarda Machado Lopes Santos, 18 anos. — Foto: Thiago Gadelha/SVM

A estudante Maria Eduarda Machado, de 18 anos, veio de Salvador para realizar a prova. O objetivo da jovem é cursar direito na USP — sonho que, segundo ela, ficou mais viável quando descobriu que poderia fazer o exame em Fortaleza.

“Ir para São Paulo fazer a prova é muito caro. Fiquei muito feliz de saber que eles iam aplicar a prova em Fortaleza, porque tenho amigos que moram aqui, então fica mais fácil de vir. Meus pais se sentem mais seguros também (...) Sei que dei o meu melhor durante o ano, estudei bastante. A gente sabe que a prova tem mudado e eu tenho me preparado para essas mudanças. Agora é colocar nas mãos de Deus e vai dar tudo certo”, afirmou.

articles.title: Onça-pintada Ibaca morre após ser resgatada com 30 kg no Pantanal | G1
articles.standfirst: Conhecida por turistas e acompanhada desde 2016, fêmea apresentou emagrecimento rápido. Causa da morte ainda é investigada.
articles.summary: Conhecida por turistas e acompanhada desde 2016, fêmea apresentou emagrecimento rápido. Causa da morte ainda é investigada.
articles.body:
A onça-pintada Ibaca, conhecida por turistas, fotógrafos e pesquisadores no Pantanal de Mato Grosso, morreu nesse sábado (31) — Foto: Rodrigo Chavez Noriega

A onça-pintada Ibaca, conhecida por turistas, fotógrafos e pesquisadores no Pantanal de Mato Grosso, morreu nesse sábado (31), após ser resgatada muito debilitada na noite anterior. A fêmea, que deixa um filhote de um ano, havia sido vista nos últimos dias com sinais de desnutrição , mas a causa da morte ainda não foi esclarecida.

Segundo o biólogo e guia de turismo Marcos Ardevino, Ibaca pesava pouco mais de 30 quilos quando foi resgatada, na sexta-feira (30). Ela teria sido transferida para Cuiabá para passar por exames, mas não resistiu.

De acordo com o biólogo, uma necropsia está sendo feita para identificar o que provocou a morte. Guias e observadores também estão reunindo vídeos registrados em diferentes datas para tentar entender como a onça emagreceu tão rapidamente.

🐆 Uma trajetória acompanhada por quase uma década

O nome da onça-pintada Ibaca tem origem tupi-guarani e significa “um céu com estrelas” — Foto: Rodrigo Chavez Noriega

Também chamada de Tina, Ibaca era acompanhada na região desde 2016. Ao longo dos anos, foi fotografada e filmada em encontros com outros animais e ao lado dos próprios filhotes, tornando-se uma das fêmeas conhecidas por quem observa a vida selvagem no Pantanal.

Segundo o Projeto Jaguar ID, ela foi observada em dez temporadas consecutivas, entre 2016 e 2025. O nome Ibaca tem origem tupi-guarani e, conforme o projeto, significa “um céu com estrelas”.

Os registros permitiram acompanhar diferentes momentos da vida da onça, especialmente a reprodução, os cuidados com os filhotes e as interações com outros animais.

O catálogo do projeto identifica Ibaca como filha da onça Overa e irmã de Saseka, Siriri e Cururu. Entre os filhotes dela registrados ao longo dos anos estão Ipepo, Jasy e Apejara. A documentação aponta filhotes identificados em temporadas como as de 2018, 2022 e 2025.

Também há registros da fêmea com parceiros reprodutivos como Xingu, Guassú, Bagua e Merlin.

Esse acompanhamento ajudou a estabelecer relações de parentesco e a documentar diferentes gerações de onças em vida livre no Pantanal.

articles.title: Criança morre após ser arrastada por correnteza em Ji-Paraná, RO | G1
articles.standfirst: Mãe não viu o menino saindo de casa e soube do acidente pelos vizinhos. Havia chovido na região.
articles.summary: O pequeno Gabriel Piscinati de Souza, de 4 anos, tinha autismo e foi localizado pelos bombeiros a 300 metros do local da queda, mas não resistiu ao acidente.
articles.body:
Um menino de quatro anos, chamado Gabriel Piscinati de Souza, morreu após cair em um igarapé e ser arrastado por uma correnteza no sábado (31), no bairro Dom Bosco, em Ji-Paraná (RO). No momento do acidente, havia chovido na região.

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, a mãe de Gabriel não percebeu quando ele acordou, levantou e saiu de casa em direção à rua. Ela só soube do desaparecimento quando vizinhos informaram que a criança havia caído no igarapé que faz divisa com a residência e não tinha sido mais vista.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, as equipes foram acionadas e, após cerca de 30 minutos de buscas, encontraram a criança a aproximadamente 300 metros do ponto onde foi vista pela última vez.

Os bombeiros realizaram os primeiros socorros e encaminharam Gabriel ao hospital, mas ele não resistiu. Segundo a corporação, o menino ficou muito tempo na água.

Gabriel tinha diagnóstico de autismo. O Movimento das Mães Atípicas de Porto Velho lamentou a morte da criança e também destacou a importância da segurança dos espaços públicos e da prevenção de acidentes.

“Que essa tragédia também nos faça refletir sobre a importância da segurança dos espaços públicos, da prevenção de acidentes e da proteção de todas as crianças, incluindo aquelas com deficiência”, diz a nota.

articles.title: Fuvest 2027: candidatos contam desafios na busca por vaga na USP | G1
articles.standfirst: Em São Carlos (SP), 2.423 candidatos estão inscritos no processo seletivo. Em todo o estado, o vestibular reúne 106.165 participantes que disputam uma vaga na USP.
articles.summary: Em São Carlos (SP), 2.423 candidatos estão inscritos no processo seletivo. Em todo o estado, o vestibular reúne 106.165 participantes que disputam uma vaga na USP.
articles.body:
Em São Carlos (SP), 2.423 candidatos estão inscritos na primeira fase da Fuvest — Foto: Claudinei Júnior/g1

Após meses de estudo e preparação, estudantes encaram neste domingo (1º) a primeira fase da Fuvest 2027. Em São Carlos (SP), 2.423 candidatos estão inscritos no vestibular , que é uma das principais portas de entrada para a Universidade de São Paulo ( USP ).

As provas são aplicadas na Escola de Engenharia, com 601 candidatos, e no Centro Universitário Central Paulista (Unicep), que recebe outros 1.822 inscritos. Na região, Pirassununga (SP) também recebe candidatos para a primeira fase, com outros 1.043 inscritos.

Em todo o estado, 106.165 candidatos participam da Fuvest 2027 . Desse total, 93.828 disputam uma das 8.147 vagas na USP, enquanto outros 12.337 fazem a prova como treineiros.

Estudantes de São Carlos (SP) falam sobre desafios e preparação para conquistar vaga na USP — Foto: Claudinei Júnior/g1

A estudante Ana Clara Pinheiro José, de 18 anos , chegou à Unicep às 10h45, mais de uma hora antes da abertura oficial dos portões, às 12h. Natural de São Carlos, ela presta o vestibular pela primeira vez e ainda está dividida entre os cursos de Biologia e Farmácia.

“Estou aqui desde as 6h da manhã preparando tudo. Cheguei adiantada porque não queria correr o risco de ficar preso na lotação”, contou.

A preparação de Ana Clara foi feita em uma escola de período integral, complementada por um cursinho noturno. Ela destacou a influência dos professores, o material de vestibular disponibilizado pela escola e o incentivo de duas primas que foram aprovadas em Farmácia.

“Desde pequenininha sonhava em estudar biologia; meus professores me motivaram, e minhas primas me inspiraram a escolher Farmácia”, disse.

A estudante Ana Clara Pinheiro José, de 18 anos, chegou chego à Unicep, em São Carlos (SP) — Foto: Claudinei Júnior/g1

Já o estudante de Araraquara (SP) Guilherme Thummel, de 18 anos , encara a Fuvest pela segunda vez. Depois de participar do vestibular anteriormente, ele chega à nova tentativa com o objetivo de conquistar uma vaga no curso de Medicina.

Para ele, as questões de Ciências da Natureza e Matemática devem estar entre os principais desafios da avaliação.

“A prova costuma ser bem conteudista, a parte mais pesada deve ser Natureza e Matemática, mas me preparei muito bem e espero fazer uma boa prova”, disse.

Para enfrentar as cinco horas de avaliação, Guilherme aposta na tranquilidade, em pequenas pausas e na fé. Para ele, estudar Medicina representa mais do que uma escolha profissional: é um “sacerdócio”.

“A USP tem um peso enorme, esse curso se destaca como um dos melhores do país. Estou mais confiante e preparado para transformar o esforço de um ano inteiro em uma vaga na segunda fase", completou.

Morador de Araraquara (SP), o estudante Guilherme Thummel, de 18 anos, encara a Fuvest pela segunda vez — Foto: Claudinei Jùnior/g1

A estudante Giovana Caneppel, de 20 anos, também participa da Fuvest pela segunda vez. O objetivo dela é conquistar uma vaga no curso de Arquitetura.

Entre os desafios da prova, ela aponta a Matemática como uma das principais preocupações, mas espera encontrar questões menos complicadas do que na edição anterior.

“Para mim, a parte mais difícil será Matemática, mas espero que não esteja tão complicada quanto no ano passado”, afirmou.

A preparação foi baseada na resolução de provas anteriores da Fuvest, além de estudos constantes ao longo do ano. Mesmo cursando Arquitetura em uma universidade particular, Giovana mantém o sonho de ingressar em uma instituição pública.

“A USP tem um peso enorme e vai acrescentar muito ao meu currículo. Sempre gostei de arquitetura, de toda a estética e arte envolvida" contou.

A estudante Giovana Caneppel, de 20 anos, também participa da Fuvest pela segunda vez — Foto: Claudinei Júnior/g1

Os portões dos locais de prova abrem às 12h e fecham às 13h . A avaliação tem duração de cinco horas , e os candidatos podem deixar os prédios a partir das 16h.

A primeira fase terá 80 questões de múltipla escolha , 10 a menos que as 90 aplicadas até o ano passado. Apesar da redução, o tempo de prova permanece o mesmo: cinco horas.

A mudança acompanha a ampliação da interdisciplinaridade do conteúdo. A proposta é priorizar questões que exijam dos candidatos a capacidade de relacionar conhecimentos de diferentes áreas.

A avaliação busca identificar habilidades importantes para a vida universitária, como leitura e interpretação de diferentes tipos de texto, além de conhecimentos básicos em ciências humanas, biológicas, exatas e língua estrangeira.

As questões abordam as disciplinas obrigatórias do Ensino Médio: Arte, Biologia, Educação Física, Filosofia, Física, Geografia, História, Inglês, Matemática, Português, Química e Sociologia. Cada questão vale um ponto.

Estudantes realizam prova do vestibular da Fuvest neste domingo (1º) — Foto: ALOISIO MAURICIO/FOTOARENA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

Os candidatos devem apresentar obrigatoriamente um documento de identificação, físico ou digital, e uma caneta esferográfica de tinta azul ou preta, com corpo transparente.

Também é permitido levar alguns itens opcionais:

Equipamentos eletrônicos, como celular, calculadora, computador, tablet, reprodutor de áudio e máquina fotográfica;

Dispositivos vestíveis, como smartwatch, óculos eletrônicos e ponto eletrônico;

Canetas hidrográficas ou outros tipos diferentes da esferográfica;

Caneta marca-texto, compasso ou lápis com tabuada;

Protetores auriculares, fones de ouvido ou similares;

Outros materiais que não sejam permitidos para a realização da prova.

articles.title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs in Speke
articles.summary: A video which shows an officer hitting a youth is a "small part of the incident", police say.
articles.body:
A police force has said it is reviewing a video which shows one of its officers punching a boy.

The footage circulated on social media shows a Merseyside Police officer punching what appears to be teenage boy three times while holding a pair of metal handcuffs in the hand he is striking him with.

The force said officers had been responding on Friday to reports of about 20 youths in the Alder Wood Avenue area of Speke, Liverpool, blocking roads with wheelie bins and "aiming fireworks at anyone who tried to remove them".

"We would like to stress that a short clip doesn't always show the full context," a Merseyside Police spokesman said.

The footage being circulated on social media - which has been viewed more than 40,000 times - begins moments before the officer strikes the boy.

It does not show anything that happened in the run-up to the incident.

Merseyside Police said youths had reportedly "smashed windows of nearby flats, tried to start fires and threatened members of the public".

In the video, the boy is punched in the stomach, chest and throat before he is handcuffed and dragged off the ground by the officer, then led to a police van.

Another teenager can be seen being pulled from the ground as he is arrested.

After a complaint was made on Saturday, the force said its professional standards team would look into the incident.

"While we look to establish the full circumstances of what happened, we would urge people not to speculate and avoid sharing rumours or misinformation," the force said in a statement published on its website.

The incident happened the night before Halloween, on what in Liverpool has become known as "Mischief Night".

"We are determined to protect our communities from the sort of appalling behaviour that we historically see at this time of year.

"We have a contempt for criminality and a commitment to cracking down on people committing serious offences in Merseyside," a force spokesman added.

articles.title: Tory leader Kemi Badenoch opposes formal British apology for slave trade, calls it a 'navel-gazing distraction'
articles.summary: Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has dismissed calls for a formal British apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, arguing it distracts from present issues and may lead to financial demands. Her comments come as Prime Minister Andy Burnham considers the possibility of an apology ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.
articles.body: Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has rejected calls for Britain to formally apologise for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, arguing that such a move would distract from present-day priorities and could lead to demands for financial compensation.Speaking to Sky News on Sunday, Badenoch criticised Prime Minister Andy Burnham's willingness to consider an official apology ahead of next week's Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda.She described the proposed apology as a “navel-gazing distraction” and questioned whether future British leaders should continue attending Commonwealth summits if discussions increasingly focus on reparations.Badenoch told the broadcaster that she was concerned an apology would encourage campaigners and Caribbean countries to seek money from Britain for its historical involvement in slavery.“What I'm worried about is that this CHOGM summit is yet another opportunity for people to start asking Britain for money because of the slave trade,” she said, adding that the Commonwealth should focus on cooperation and future priorities rather than historical disputes.She also ruled out financial compensation for slavery, arguing that an apology could become a starting point for further demands.“I don't think we should be giving any money to compensate people for the slave trade, and I don't think that Burnham needs to be apologising because it is a lever to wedge open the door to ask for cash,” she said.In a separate social media post, Badenoch argued that discussions about slavery should acknowledge the involvement of people from different regions, including African kingdoms and merchants who captured and sold enslaved people.“Slavery was an evil in which people from every continent and region participated,” she wrote.She also referred to Britain's role in ending the transatlantic slave trade, arguing that its historical record should be considered in full rather than through selected episodes.Badenoch said a previous statement by former prime minister Tony Blair, who expressed Britain's “deep sorrow and regret” over its involvement in the slave trade nearly two decades ago, should be sufficient. She maintained that another formal apology was unnecessary.Her remarks came after Burnham said he was open to the possibility of a formal apology for Britain's role in the trafficking and enslavement of Africans. In an article published in The Guardian, he said he wanted to establish a dialogue with countries affected by the trade but ruled out direct financial reparations.Instead, Burnham proposed exploring ways to help poorer countries restructure their debt on more favourable terms, allowing them to manage repayments more effectively.He also argued that people living in Britain today should not be held financially responsible for historical actions in which they had no personal involvement, while acknowledging the scale of the suffering caused by the slave trade.The debate has gained renewed attention ahead of the Commonwealth summit, where Caribbean leaders are expected to raise the issue of reparatory justice. King Charles III is also visiting the region ahead of the meeting. During his tour, he has referred to the suffering caused by slavery and visited a site in Guyana associated with a rebellion by enslaved people against British authorities.The British government has not issued a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade or agreed to pay reparations. Burnham's proposal has reopened discussion over whether Britain should formally acknowledge its historical responsibility, even without offering financial compensation.You use AI every day. articles.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine struck Russian defence facility in Rostov
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Sunday said Kyiv had struck a Russian defence industry facility in the Rostov region, targeting an enterprise
articles.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Sunday said Kyiv had struck a Russian defence industry facility in the Rostov region, targeting an enterprise involved in missile production, as the war between the two countries continued.In a post on X, Zelenskyy said the Kamensky Combine had been hit along with two Russian air defence assets, a Pantsir-S2 system and a command and staff vehicle of the S-400 Triumf system. He estimated the total value of the damaged air defence equipment at around $70 million.“Our long-range sanctions have targeted the Rostov region. The Kamensky Combine, a Russian defence industry enterprise involved in missile production, was hit. A Pantsir-S2 system and a command and staff vehicle of the S-400 Triumf system were also hit. The total value of the air defence assets struck is around USD 70 million,” Zelenskyy wrote.He thanked Ukraine's Security Service and other units of the Defence Forces for carrying out the operation, saying Kyiv was responding to Russian aggression.“I thank the warriors of the Security Service of Ukraine @ServiceSsu and other units of the Defence Forces for their accuracy! We are justly defending ourselves against Russian aggression and doing everything to reduce Russia's capability to continue it,” he said.The claims about the strikes and the extent of the damage were not independently verified.In a separate post, Zelenskyy said Russian attacks had damaged energy infrastructure in four Ukrainian regions — Dnipro, Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr and Khmelnytskyi, leaving hundreds of thousands of families without electricity.“Overnight alone, our energy infrastructure came under Russian attack in four regions: Dnipro, Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, and Khmelnytskyi. Substations, transformers, and power lines that supply electricity to our people's homes were targeted. Repair crews are working everywhere. As of now, hundreds of thousands of families remain without power. Massive Russian attacks on Ukraine's other critical infrastructure are also continuing unabated,” he wrote.The Ukrainian president said Russia had launched 1,940 attack drones, more than 1,580 guided aerial bombs and 44 missiles of various types against Ukraine over the past week. Of the missiles, 36 were ballistic, he said.“This past week Russia has launched 1,940 attack drones, more than 1,580 guided aerial bombs, and 44 missiles of various types against Ukraine, including 36 ballistic missiles. The intensity of the strikes is extremely high, and the Russians are trying to take maximum advantage of the shortage of ballistic missile interceptors,” Zelenskyy said.Zelenskyy urged Ukraine's international partners to expedite the delivery of additional air defence systems and ammunition, particularly Patriot missiles.“Every day, we communicate our need for Patriot missiles to America, Europe, and other partners who can help. And this month, the United States and European countries made new decisions on additional packages for Ukraine. But these deliveries cannot take years. Russia is destroying infrastructure and killing our people right now, and it is betting on ballistic missiles this winter. Accordingly, decisions on air defense must also be implemented now. I thank everyone who supports the defence of Ukrainian skies,” he wrote.Kyiv is set to receive 500 PAC-3 interceptors from the United States.Meanwhile, amid efforts to revive negotiations, Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said Russian President Vladimir Putin had never refused to hold talks with Zelenskyy, ANI reported.Asked by Russian outlet Vesti whether Putin would answer a call from the Ukrainian president, Ushakov said: “I think he would answer, of course. articles.title: New airfare rules from next year: No govt intervention except in ‘extraordinary situations’ to prevent spikes
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India has adopted new airfare rules where government will not interfere in the process except “in an extraordinary situation (where) it
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India has adopted new airfare rules where government will not interfere in the process except “in an extraordinary situation (where) it considers it necessary to do so in the public interest.” Notified under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026, which will be applicable from Jan 1, 2027, government has continued its policy of letting market forces determine airfares without government interference.TOI reported on Oct 17 that India has no plans to regulate or cap airfares in the free market under which airlines here operate under the new airfare policy being finalised. However, it will keep a “strong lever” on airlines to ensure they don’t resort to very sharp surges in “exceptional and extraordinary circumstances” that see demand rising for certain routes.“Every air transport undertaking… shall establish tariff based on factors including cost of operation…. (They) shall submit tariff to the Director General (DGCA) in such form, manner and periodicity as may be specified…. (They) shall publish tariff on their websites… for wider public awareness and transparency,” says the gazette notification published Saturday (October 31).Airlines have been asked to give a break-up of tariff in terms of the total amount payable by a passenger and break-up of the same by displaying components like base fare, tax, fees, cancellation charges, refund conditions and any other charge separately.Regarding intervention in “extraordinary circumstances,” it says: “Where the central government is of the opinion that (in) an extraordinary situation it may, by order in writing, issue such directions in public interest…. such directions shall be proportionate to the circumstances and shall remain in force for the period specified only.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Trump dangles $15 billion lifeline to farmers as US midterms loom
articles.summary: The Donald Trump administration has announced more than $15 billion in payments, loans and other support for US farmers in the weeks before the midterm
articles.body: The Donald Trump administration has announced more than $15 billion in payments, loans and other support for US farmers in the weeks before the midterm elections, seeking to ease the impact of soaring fuel and fertiliser costs. The measures, announced by the US Department of Agriculture (USDA), come as farmers struggle with higher expenses linked largely to Trump's tariffs and the war in Iran. The move is also aimed at supporting agricultural producers in rural states where traditionally Republican seats are becoming competitive.Trump is scheduled to visit Iowa and Kansas on Sunday, two days before the election, as he steps up his focus on rural voters. However, it remains unclear whether the financial assistance will encourage more farmers and other rural voters to turn out in support of Republican candidates.More than half of the announced $15 billion package will go towards an $8 billion one-time payment programme for farmers facing a sharp rise in diesel prices. The USDA said it would release further details this month. However, it has not specified when farmers will receive the money.The package also includes at least $5 billion in guaranteed loans for ranchers and fishermen. Another $1.8 billion will go to producers and landowners enrolled in conservation programmes. The USDA has allocated $573 million for fertiliser manufacturing projects and $57 million to expand meat processing capacity. Specialty crop producers will receive $86.6 million in grants for innovative projects.Separately, the department plans to purchase up to $472.5 million worth of agricultural commodities to support producers and supply charitable programmes.These initiatives come in addition to $13.8 billion in safety net payments planned for eligible farmers for the 2025 crop year. The payments are intended to cover financial shortfalls for producers of key crops, including corn, soybeans, wheat and rice.The USDA has also announced measures to expand sales of diesel normally restricted to off-road use, improve transparency in cattle sale data and strengthen wolf management policies to protect livestock.Farmers face rising costsThe financial assistance comes after a difficult year for US farmers, who have faced rising fuel and fertiliser costs, alongside higher expenses for agricultural equipment due to tariffs imposed last year. The trade war with China also led to a near boycott of US agricultural goods.Diesel prices have been a particular concern. On Friday, the average price stood at $6.32 per gallon, slightly below its September peak but 70% higher than a year earlier, according to motor club AAA. Filling a 100-gallon tank now costs farmers around $260 more than it did a year ago.Gregg Ibendahl, a farm management specialist at Kansas State University, said the payments could more than compensate for the increase in fuel costs and help farmers deal with expensive fertiliser.He said: “That input side risk, I think, is the thing that really has hurt farmers this year, as well as the fact that there has been a lot more uncertainty about what’s going to happen in the world,”Ibendahl expects the additional payments to help farmers who might otherwise fail to make a profit this year. However, he cautioned that temporary government assistance would not address the wider problems driving up production costs.“It’s hard to go to your lender in the next spring and say, ‘OK, well, we’re looking pretty good this year, but it’s all because of these extra temporary government payments, so how much can you make me a loan (for) next year for my crop?’” he said.Alexandra Middlewood, an associate professor of political science at Wichita State University, said farmers have expressed mixed reactions to the assistance. While many welcome the support that could help keep their businesses afloat, some view the programmes as one-time bailouts rather than a long-term solution.Rural voters and the midterm electionsThe agricultural sector has traditionally been an important source of support for Trump, particularly in rural states. However, some of his policies have also affected farmers and businesses dependent on the agricultural economy.Michael Smith, a political science professor at Emporia State University, said immigration deportations have threatened the agricultural labour force. Cuts to foreign aid and food assistance programmes such as SNAP have also affected the market for agricultural products.“Some people who admire Trump really just admire the person, the man,” he said. “But it doesn’t mean they necessarily like his policies. Well, Trump himself isn’t on the ballot this year. His policies are.”Middlewood said the cost of living and access to healthcare remain major concerns among rural voters. She added that there is a perception that the administration has not done enough to address these issues, despite Trump's claims at campaign rallies about a booming economy.She does not expect dissatisfied rural voters in Kansas to shift towards the Democratic Party, given the state's long-standing Republican leanings. However, some could choose not to vote or support independent candidates, potentially affecting Republican prospects.“Independent voters make or break elections," she said. "And so that’s really what it’s going to come down to this year is those independent voters and who they’re breaking for.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: France opens ‘attempted murder’ probe into petrol bomb attacks on police
articles.summary: No arrests made after several security officers were reportedly injured during incidents at Saturday’s protests.
articles.body:
Prosecutors in France have launched an investigation into attempted murder after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during protests in Paris, as video of an officer in flames provoked outrage.

The probe announced on Sunday came after the Paris police prefecture said several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail.

On Saturday, clashes erupted in Paris and other cities as hundreds of thousands of people staged a third weekend of protests against soaring living costs and deteriorating public services.

Video and images from the demonstrations showed a homemade incendiary device exploding at the feet of a security officer in protective gear, engulfing his lower body in flames.

Prosecutors said the investigation was opened for “attempted murder of persons vested with public authority”.

“Explosive devices were thrown at around 15 gendarmes as well as police officers,” the prosecutor’s office said, referring to military police officers who are part of the French armed forces.

While riots were less widespread than two weeks ago , when France experienced some of its worst unrest in years, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Saturday that the level of violence perpetrated by some was “extraordinary”.

An assessment of the injured was ongoing, prosecutors said, adding that the reported injuries included second-degree burns.

The gendarme struck said his unit was “under assault”, with glass bottles, paving stones, shards of glass and firebombs thrown at them.

“We were hit by several significant incendiary devices,” he told broadcaster RTL on condition of anonymity.

“The flammable substance was so greasy that I could feel it spreading across my skin,” he said. “I kept wondering when it would stop because I really felt as though I had been coated by the heat itself.”

The officer, who received minor injuries, said the leg and shin protections on his riot uniform melted.

The gendarmerie said 13 members of the officer’s unit were injured, according to RTL.

No suspects “have been arrested at this stage in connection with the incident”, the prosecutor’s office said, adding that investigators were working to identify those responsible.

More than 770 people were arrested across France, the interior ministry said.

A total of 159 members of law enforcement were injured during protests and Halloween celebrations, it added.

The protests come in a tense political climate, with presidential elections six months away and far-right frontrunner Marine Le Pen vowing to restore law and order if elected next year.

Le Pen, the leader of the far-right National Rally party, said on X that those responsible for the firebomb attack must be “punished with the utmost severity”.

articles.title: A billionaire gave $160 million to transform a 158-year-old dinosaur museum; in 2024, it reopened with bigger galleries and free entry
articles.summary: Yale Peabody Museum, now free to all, reopens after a $160 million renovation enhancing its dinosaur exhibits and educational facilities.
articles.body: Natural history museums serve two purposes: they preserve scientific collections for research and make discoveries about the natural world accessible to the public. The Yale Peabody Museum in New Haven, Connecticut, brought these roles together after a major renovation. It reopened on March 26, 2024, following four years of work, with expanded galleries, restored dinosaur displays, new educational facilities and free admission for every visitor. The reopening marked a major change for a museum that had been an important part of Yale's scientific and educational work for more than a century.The renovation was inspired by a $160 million donation from Yale alumni and billionaire benefactor Edward P. Bass, Connecticut public radio station WSHU reported. Yale revealed the donation in 2018, and the university says it is the largest known gift to a natural history museum in the U.S. The museum dates to 1866; thus, it was 158 years old when its doors reopened, and Yale Peabody Museum affirmed in November 2021 that entry will remain free in perpetuity when the construction is complete.A bigger museum with more to seeThe museum had not undergone a major renovation in nearly a century. Designed by Centerbrook Architects and Planners, the project expanded exhibition space by more than 50% and spread the galleries across three floors instead of two. Classroom space tripled, and the museum gained a new education centre for schoolchildren from the New Haven area. New imaging, sound and 3D printing studios allow students to work hands-on with selected objects from the museum's collection, which contains around 14 million specimens and artefacts. The third floor galleries, including the David Friend Hall mineral and gem gallery, opened on a phased schedule after the March reopening.Dinosaurs remain a major attraction, and their displays received substantial changes during the renovation. Yale reported that the museum's famous dinosaur and prehistoric mammal fossils had been cleaned, repaired and remounted in poses reflecting current scientific understanding of these animals as active creatures. The displays include the first specimens of Brontosaurus, Stegosaurus and Triceratops ever discovered. The 65-foot Brontosaurus once again dominates the Burke Hall of Dinosaurs. Its tail was lengthened and raised to allow visitors to walk beneath it, while its head and neck were repositioned in a more alert, birdlike pose.Other displays also draw attention. In the new Central Gallery, a suspended scene depicts Archelon, the largest known sea turtle, appearing to flee a hungry mosasaur above visitors' heads. The American mastodon is now displayed with its tusks raised and exposed rather than in profile behind glass. A second-floor gallery features scientific instruments from the museum's History of Science and Technology Collection, including Yale's first microscope, purchased in 1734. Museum ambassadors help visitors understand the exhibits, while revised labels make the displays more accessible to a wider audience. But size and spectacle are only half the story. The other half is who gets through the door.Free admission changes who comesBefore the renovation, the Peabody charged an admission fee, unlike the Yale University Art Gallery and the Yale Centre for British Art, which already offered free public entry. The new policy brought the Peabody into line with those institutions and removed the admission cost for visitors from New Haven, the wider Connecticut community and beyond.Museum director David Skelly described free admission as one part of a wider effort to make the institution more accessible and welcoming. “Free admission is a means, not the end,” he said when Yale announced the policy. The renovation also improved access through redesigned galleries, clearer exhibit labels and museum ambassadors who help visitors understand the displays. New classrooms and a student-curated exhibition space further connect the museum's public role with teaching and research at Yale.Those planning a trip should note that individual visitors do not need a ticket or a booked time slot, according to the museum’s website. It is open Tuesday to Friday 10 a.m.- 5 p.m. and Saturday and Sunday noon-5 pm and closed on Mondays at the time of writing. School and group visits by appointment only. The museum is located at 170 Whitney Avenue in New Haven. Yale had a reservation system for the first 30 days to control crowds at launch and has since moved to walk-in visitation.The Peabody's reopening changed more than its galleries. Its restored fossil displays, expanded educational facilities, and wider access to the collections reflect a renewed emphasis on both public learning and scientific research. By making admission permanently free, the museum also opened its doors to visitors who might previously have been put off by the cost of entry.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: Department of Homeland Security general counsel James Percival vowed to find, charge and deport noncitizens who cast illegal ballots in midterm elections.

"Some of them have criminal histories that include assault with a dangerous weapon, domestic violence, drug trafficking, burglary, and driving under the influence. In October, Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs challenged findings from the Justice Department last week after federal officials said investigators had identified more than 400 noncitizens illegally registered to vote in the state, some of whom they said had cast ballots in multiple elections dating back decades. Hobbs pushed back against the findings, saying the state's review of the list uncovered "several glaring deficiencies." "This list includes United States citizens and is not reliable. articles.title: ‘Heat’ director Michael Mann injured in accidental weapon discharge at L.A. gun range
articles.summary: The “Heat” director was briefly treated at the hospital, a representative for the filmmaker said.
articles.body: “Heat” director Michael Mann was hospitalized this weekend after an accidental gun discharge at a gun range in Los Angeles. The incident resulted in a minor, subcutaneous injury to Mann, according to a representative for the Emmy Award-winning filmmaker. Mann, 83, has been a target shooter for decades and was practicing at the range when the accident occurred. “On Saturday, at a gun range, a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered resulting in a superficial injury to film director Michael Mann,” his representative said in a statement. “He was treated and is being released.” The Los Angeles Police Department also confirmed that officers who responded to a radio call of shots fired at the location on Saturday determined that the shooting was accidental. The subject was transported to a local hospital in stable condition, a spokesperson said, and the LAPD cleared the scene after completing an injury report. Mann is best known for his crime dramas, including his 1981 feature debut “Thief,” the 1986 thriller “Manhunter” and the 1995 crime epic “Heat.” He told Vulture in 2017 that the cast of “Heat” shot full-load blanks to re-create the sound of real gunfire rather than relying on edited sound effects. “That’s the sound the weapons actually made and you couldn’t imitate or improve upon them,” Mann said. “It was terrifying as hell because we were in these glass and steel canyons and the gunfire reverberated in a certain real way, so they had an authenticity to the place that really was unique.” Mann is reportedly developing “Heat 2” as an adaptation of his 2022 novel of the same name, which he co-wrote with Meg Gardiner.

articles.title: Alaska family has owned a 115-acre farm since 1948; as housing spreads nearby, they make sure the land can never be divided for development
articles.summary: The Grover family has safeguarded their 115-acre farm in Alaska, ensuring it remains protected from housing development through a permanent conservation easement, preserving essential agricultural land for future generations.
articles.body: Housing and agriculture compete for productive land throughout southcentral Alaska's Matanuska Valley. As Palmer grows, development increasingly puts pressure on farmland that could otherwise remain in agricultural production. It is extremely rare for a field to resume producing food after it has been paved over and built on. In June 2025, one local family took steps to protect its farm from that possibility.The 115.22 acre Grover Farm in Palmer was permanently protected through an agricultural conservation easement that closed on June 13, 2025. Clifton and Vera Grover established the farm in 1948, and their family still owns the property. Under the agreement, the family received financial compensation for permanently giving up development rights, meaning the land cannot be subdivided or paved over for housing. The project involved the Alaska Farmland Trust and the US Department of Agriculture's Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS). Wesley Grover said he had spent about five years working with the trust to secure the agreementA family farm since 1948The Grovers' story began in November 1948, when Clifton and Vera Grover moved to the Matanuska Valley and began farming the property. Wesley Grover recalled that the family initially planted oats, peas and vetch, which they used for hay and silage. He described the soil as excellent and stressed its importance to farming. "You need the land to plant the crops, you can't get that any place, they don't make any more of it," he said.Over the decades, the farm changed with the family's circumstances. It began as a dairy operation and later shifted to cattle production. The family also started leasing portions of the property to other local farmers, allowing the land to remain in agricultural use as the operation evolved.The trust’s board president, Leslie Senden, says the property holds about 15 feet of topsoil and sits close to markets, which makes it well placed for food production. Senden also counts it among the best soils in the state on the Springer system in Palmer. At the signing ceremony, Wesley and his wife Bonnie were joined by four of their grown children. A signature, though, is only the start of the story. What keeps the promise in force is the legal tool behind it.How the easement worksThe Alaska Farmland Trust's voluntary programme allows landowners to retain ownership while permanently giving up specified development rights. The Grover family still owns the farm, but it can no longer be divided into residential lots or paved over for housing. Agricultural activities can continue under the terms of the easement.Federal support for agricultural easements comes through the Agricultural Conservation Easement Program (ACEP). Its Agricultural Land Easement component helps protect working farms by limiting nonagricultural development. For eligible projects, NRCS may contribute up to 50 per cent of the fair market value of the agricultural land easement. The programme works with land trusts and other eligible partners that hold and manage these agreements.The easement remains effective beyond the current owners' lifetimes. Future owners will also have to follow its restrictions if the property changes hands. The Alaska Farmland Trust monitors protected properties at least once a year to check that land use complies with each agreement. If a violation occurs, the organisation can take steps to enforce the restrictions.Why Palmer’s farmland mattersDevelopment pressure continues to affect farmland across the Matanuska Valley. Margaret Adsit, the trust's lands coordinator, said agricultural properties were increasingly being converted into housing and other nonagricultural uses. "The time to act is now. Once it's gone, it's gone for good," she said.When the Grover easement closed in June 2025, the Alaska Farmland Trust had protected 519 acres in total as it marked its 20th anniversary. The 115.22-acre Grover Farm therefore accounted for more than a fifth of the acreage the organisation had conserved at that time. The trust also operates its FarmLink programme, which connects farmland owners with aspiring farmers to help keep protected properties in active agricultural use.The easement also has a food supply dimension. Alaska Farmland Trust board president Leslie Senden said the farm has about 15 feet of topsoil and lies close to markets, making it suitable for continued food production. The trust and NRCS described its protection as part of a broader effort to keep productive agricultural land available to feed future generations of Alaskans. For the Grover family, the agreement protects more than seven decades of agricultural history. The property remains privately owned, but its development rights have been permanently retired, allowing future generations to keep using the land for farming rather than residential construction.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1913, an Ohio couple sent their eight-month-old son to his grandmother through the postal service; the baby weighed just under the parcel limit and the journey cost only 15 cents
articles.summary: Back in the olden days, travel wasn't as cheap and convenient as it is today. So, parents had to get a little creative to save a quick buck.
articles.body: Back in the olden days, travel wasn't as cheap and convenient as it is today. So, parents had to get a little creative to save a quick buck. But one child's parents took penny-pinching a bit too far.In January 1913, Jesse and Mathilda Beagle of Ohio found an unusual way to send their eight-month-old son, James, to his grandmother's house. Instead of buying a train ticket, the couple took advantage of the newly introduced US Postal Service's Parcel Post system. They paid 15 cents in postage, insured their son for $50 and handed him over to the mail carrier for delivery. The grandmother lived only a few miles away in Batavia, making it a relatively short journey for the infant. James weighed just under 11 pounds, narrowly meeting the weight limit for parcels accepted by the postal service.What sounds like quite a turbulent trip now, was a rather unusual interpretation of the postal service's new rules back then.How children became parcelsWhen the US Postal Service introduced its Parcel Post service on January 1, 1913, Americans could suddenly send packages weighing more than four pounds through the mail. This was a game changer for those rural communities, which had limited access to shops and private delivery services. However, the regulations surrounding what could and could not be posted were not particularly clear in the early days.People began testing the limits of the new service, sending everything from eggs and bricks to snakes and other unusual items. With no explicit regulation prohibiting the mailing of human beings, some parents saw an opportunity to send their children to relatives at a fraction of the cost of a passenger train ticket.Between 1913 and 1915, historians at the Smithsonian's National Postal Museum identified approximately seven instances of children being sent through the US postal system. While the practice was hardly widespread, it occasionally made newspaper headlines, particularly when children travelled considerable distances.The journeys were not always as alarming as they sound. In rural America, postal workers were often familiar faces in their communities, known to the families along their delivery routes. Some parents entrusted their children to carriers they knew personally, rather than handing them over to complete strangers. The children were also not necessarily stuffed into mailbags alongside parcels. They were sometimes accompanied by postal employees, particularly when travelling by railway mail.The little girl who travelled 73 milesOne of the most well-known instances involved six-year-old May Pierstorff from Grangeville, Idaho. On February 19, 1914, her parents arranged for her to travel approximately 73 miles by railway mail to visit her grandparents.Her parents paid 53 cents in postage, attaching the stamps to her coat before handing her over to the postal service. Fortunately, May was accompanied by a relative who worked as a clerk for the Railway Mail Service, making the journey considerably safer than it might otherwise have been. Her story eventually became so well known that it inspired the children's book Mailing May.The incident, however, caught the attention of Postmaster General Albert S. Burleson. Alongside another inquiry about sending children through the mail that month, May's journey prompted him to formally prohibit postal workers from accepting human beings as mail.The new restriction did not immediately put an end to the practice. In 1915, a woman in Florida managed to send her six-year-old daughter approximately 720 miles to her grandfather's home in Virginia. The journey became the longest known instance of a child being transported through the US postal system, with postage costing just 15 cents.The last recorded postal delivery of a childIn August 1915, three-year-old Maud Smith made what appears to be the last successful journey of a child through the US postal service. Her grandparents arranged for her to travel approximately 40 miles across Kentucky to visit her sick mother.The incident attracted newspaper attention and prompted an investigation by John Clark, superintendent of the Cincinnati division of the Railway Mail Service. He questioned how the postmaster in Caney, Kentucky, had permitted a child to board a mail train despite the recently introduced restrictions.Although the exact consequences for the local postmaster remain unclear, the incident brought further attention to the need for stricter enforcement of postal regulations.Even years later, some parents continued to enquire about sending their children through the mail. In June 1920, First Assistant Postmaster General John C. Koons rejected two such applications, clarifying that children could not be classified as harmless live animals eligible for postal transportation.When the postman was more than a delivery personWhile the idea of sending children through the mail might seem like a rather alarming example of parental penny-pinching, it also reveals something about rural American communities in the early 20th century.Postal workers were often among the few people who visited remote households regularly. They delivered letters, parcels and essential supplies, but their responsibilities could extend well beyond their official duties. Familiar with the families on their routes, some carriers helped during medical emergencies, assisted with deliveries and checked on people who lived alone.The introduction of Parcel Post had been intended to make goods and services more accessible, particularly to people living far from commercial centres. Instead, its loosely defined early regulations briefly opened the door to some rather unexpected deliveries. The postal service eventually tightened its rules, but the stories of children travelling hundreds of miles with stamps pinned to their clothes remain a curious footnote in American postal history.Maybe now if your kids ask you where babies come from, saying through post won't be completely false.You use AI every day. articles.title: Holiday airfare hits 10-year high as Thanksgiving and Christmas travel costs soar
articles.summary: Prices of holiday plane travel are averaging $402 for Thanksgiving and $452 for Christmas as elevated jet fuel costs drive prices to 10-year highs, per Hopper.
articles.body: Holiday airfares are reaching 10-year highs this year, putting added pressure on Americans planning Thanksgiving and Christmas trips. But a travel expert says there are still ways to save. Hopper, a travel-booking company, published its 2026 Holiday Travel Index revealing sharp increases in airfare prices compared to last year. The report analyzed a week's worth of flight searches in September, focusing on lower-priced tickets and accounting for changes in Thanksgiving's date when comparing prices to last year. POPULAR US AIRPORT CALLED OUT AS 'MOST STRESSFUL' IN AMERICA FOR TRAVELERS The data shows that domestic round-trip airfare for Thanksgiving is averaging $402, up 31% ($95) from last year. International airfare has also increased, particularly for popular destinations in Europe, Mexico and Central America. For Christmas, domestic round-trip airfare is averaging $452, up 23% ($85) from last year. Flights to Mexico and Central America have increased 23%, while fares to Europe are up 15%. Hopper attributed the rising price to elevated jet fuel costs. "Travelers looking ahead to Thanksgiving and Christmas travel will need to plan ahead for a larger travel budget this year, as the 2026 holiday travel is on track to be the most expensive in a decade," the report said. POPULAR AIRLINE HITS CUSTOMERS WITH STEEP FEE HIKE FOR FIRST TIME IN 8 YEARS "Months of elevated jet fuel costs due to the conflict in Iran have contributed to Thanksgiving and Christmas airfares reaching 10-year highs." Gary Leff, a Texas-based aviation expert who founded the blog "View from the Wing," told Fox News Digital that the higher prices will heavily impact families traveling together. "It's a much bigger deal when you're multiplying increases by, you know, four or more passengers," Leff said. Leff suggests travelers continue monitoring airfare prices after booking, as they may be able to recover some of the difference if prices fall. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "You buy now and the fare drops, you just have to watch it," he suggested. "Don't just buy it and then never look again." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "As long as you're not buying a basic economy ticket, most tickets no longer have change fees," Leff said. "What that means is that you can call up the airline and apply your old ticket to a new one and generally get a credit back for the difference." "Most tickets no longer have change fees." Leff also said common money-saving strategies, such as flying out of a different airport or booking a connecting flight, don't always work. "If you're looking at an alternate airport that's farther away, there are costs for driving," he said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "You may [have] to park where you otherwise wouldn't, or somebody might drop you off or wouldn't, or the Uber is more expensive." He said choosing a connecting flight over a nonstop route can introduce additional risks, particularly during the busy holiday season. "If you take a connection instead of a nonstop, that's more of an opportunity for things to go wrong," Leff said.
