articles.title: Plane crash near Greenacres killed all nine people aboard, U.S. says
articles.summary: Officials confirm that the plane that crashed near Greenacres on Sunday had nine onboard and was coming from Texas and heading to the Bahamas.
articles.body:
Federal authorities said that the plane crash Sunday near Greenacres was a Learjet with nine people aboard and had departed Austin, Texas and was headed to the Bahamas.

The plane crashed into a mobile home neighborhood around 12:50 p.m. in the area of Military Trail and 10th Avenue North, causing major destruction, including fires and scattered debris.

All nine people aboard the plane died, Sean Duffy, the U.S. secretary of transportation, said in a post on X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, made just before 4 p.m. He called the crash a "horrific tragedy."

The FAA said the Learjet 60 departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas.

The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board will investigate. The NTSB will be in charge of the investigation and will provide all updates.

The incident closed all lanes of Military Trail in the area of Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North, the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office said.

Authorities said motorists should are avoid the area and seek alternate routes.

Postings on Facebook show a fairly wide swath of area spotted with fires, debris and what looks like a crater in the ground.

A video circulating online of a plane making a nosedive into the ground is said to be the Learjet, but The Palm Beach Post is not sharing that video as it has not been confirmed. The video is said to be from a driver's dashcam video.

The cause of the crash is unknown. Some chatter on social media raised the suspicion that the plane could have been shot down because flight restrictions were in place as President Donald Trump was in town this weekend . Trump departed President Donald J. Trump International Airport for Iowa around noon.

The Palm Beach Post reported recently that military air defense systems have been positioned around the president's Mar-a-Lago club and home and the surrounding area. Planes that fly into the restricted airspace are diverted, usually by military jets. Multiple planes have violated the airspace since Trump first took office, but a plane has never been shot down in Palm Beach County because of the airspace violations.

The upgraded security systems, a pair of Avenger Air Defense Systems , are positioned on a floating barge in the Lake Worth Lagoon on the west side of the seawall next to Trump's Mar-a-Lago. A separate bank of Avenger Air Defense Systems are positioned on the south side of Trump international airport, near the area where Air Force One parks during Trump's visits to Palm Beach.

Each Avenger comprises a modified Humvee equipped with a rotating turret that has two pods capable of launching short-range infrared-homing Stinger missiles, according to a U.S. Army website. The Avenger's targets could include cruise missiles, drones, helicopters and low-flying and high-speed fixed-wing aircraft, according to the Army.

As of Sunday night, there was no indication the Learjet was shot down.

Weather conditions in the West Palm Beach area on Sunday afternoon were overcast with rain and lightning in the area and winds from the east at 15 mph, gusting to near 25 mph. The National Weather Service in Miami said visibility was 7 miles.

The crash site is in an unincorporated area near Greenacres and Palm Springs.

The Village of Palm Springs said it has officials on the scene monitoring any effect the crash will have on water and sewer services. If residents experience disruptions, they should call the Utilities Department at (561) 584-8200.

Check back for updates on this Breaking News story.

articles.title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends
articles.summary: A rare humanitarian ceasefire allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.
articles.body:
A rare humanitarian ceasefire in Ukraine's front-line Kherson region that allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky has ended.

The localised ceasefire was due to end at 22:59 Ukrainian time (21:00 GMT) on Sunday. While the truce had held since it was implemented last week, fighting had continued elsewhere.

On Sunday evening, Ukraine's air alert system was apparently hacked, the country's air force said, warning of radiation over Kyiv - a reference to a possible nuclear attack.

The Air Force message read: "The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel."

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had struck energy infrastructure in four regions overnight on Saturday, leaving hundreds of thousands of homes without power. Some connections were restored on Sunday.

Another overnight strike killed two people, including a 13-year-old girl, in the Vinnytsia region, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said.

Meanwhile, Ukraine hit a major missile fuel producer in Russia's Rostov region, which caused a fire and damaged four production facilities, Zelensky said.

In Ukraine, repair works to restore power continued throughout the day. Most customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region had their connections restored by early evening, but more than 60,000 were still without power, the governor said.

Because of regular attacks on energy infrastructure, emergency power cuts have been introduced across the country. Even in the capital Kyiv, electricity is cut off for most of the day, and water supplies are also disrupted.

Zelensky said in a social media post that the intensity of Russian strikes has been "extremely high" over the past week, adding that Russia was "trying to take maximum advantage of the shortage of ballistic missile interceptors".

He added that "every day" Ukraine communicated its need for Patriot missiles - the only effective weapon for downing Russia's deadly ballistic missiles - to the US, Europe and other partners. He thanked countries for their support so far and longer-term commitments, but called again for more immediate aid.

The limited pause in hostilities, which started on Tuesday, was brokered with the help of US First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo.

It was originally confined to the city of Oleshky, which has been occupied by Russia since the first days of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and was expanded across the wider region of Kherson.

Oleshky had been trapped on one side by the Dnipro river and the other by Russian forces, with routes out mined and subject to drone attack.

Residents trapped there were suffering severe shortages of food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.

The truce allowed for Oleskhy residents to evacuate if they wanted, and there were emotional scenes on Saturday of reunions between loved ones who hadn't seen eachother for years.

There are Ukrainian military positions just 5km (3.1 miles) from Oleshky, but evacuees had to travel through Russian-occupied territory to southern Russia, where they flew to Belarus, before finally being driven across Ukraine's northern border.

The oldest evacuee was 94 years old, while the youngest was one, according to Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman.

articles.title: Biological male competing in girls' cross-country race denies another runner and her team a trip to state
articles.summary: A biological male runner on Camas High's girls' cross-country team displaced a Puyallup girl from state, fueling debate ahead of Initiative 638.
articles.body: UNIVERSITY PLACE, Wash. — When the Camas High cross-country runner's name was called, Joel Retzlaff yelled, "That's a man!" Retzlaff is the outspoken father of Skyview High cross-country runner Sierra Retzlaff, who has publicly opposed competing against a biological male. But as Joel made that declaration, nobody walked up to the podium. The Camas boy, who switched to the girls' team midseason, was nowhere to be found. Camas coach Matt LeGrand — who's in an impossible position — would not comment on why. But there's a decent chance the runner didn't want to face a crowd who knew that, by finishing seventh in regionals, he prevented an actual girl from advancing to state. DAD BANNED FROM SCHOOL GROUNDS AFTER PROTESTING TRANS RUNNER COMPETING AGAINST HIS DAUGHTER We won't mention that girl's name here, but she ran for Puyallup High — which finished eighth in the girls' 4A division. The top seven teams go on to state, and if not for the Camas runner's contribution, Puyallup would have advanced. That team's coach also wouldn’t comment. Understandable. This is the story that, on Halloween, had almost everybody involved spooked. The key word above is "almost," because there were some people at that meet at Chambers Bay who were willing to speak up. One of them was Carol Brown, a three-time Olympian who won a bronze medal in rowing who can't believe she's on the front lines for an issue she thought was settled a half century ago. "I fought for Title IX to be allowed to be in sports period, and so I've been fighting this battle. I never thought 50 years later I'd be fighting it again," Brown said. "And I absolutely believe in rights for everyone to participate in sport, but for it to be fair and safe, it has to be based on sex." What do you think about this Camas runner displacing another girl? "It's absolutely unfair," Brown said. "The girls put in work, and what I find the hardest to accept is that everyone is saying the girls' voices don't matter, their emotions don't matter, their hard work and once again, like 100 years ago took a second seat to the males." WASHINGTON GIRLS WALK OFF CROSS COUNTRY MEET IN PROTEST OF MALE ATHLETE, PARENTS REVEAL HOW IT CAME TO THIS The Camas runner started the season on the boys' team, where he finished 76th in the season's opening JV meet. After switching to the girls' team, he has won a varsity meet and finished second three times. In the past two meets — first at districts last week and again at regionals Saturday — he placed just ahead of Skyview runner Charlie Garrett. Safe to say Garrett wasn't happy about that. "I mean, it's really frustrating. I was sad after my race because I was less than a second away [from beating the Camas runner]," said Garrett, admitting that beating him was a side goal of hers Saturday. "But I PR'd, and I qualified for state, so I shouldn't be sad." What do you think about him not showing up on the podium? "It shows why he shouldn't be in it," Garrett said. "He has a reason not to show up." But plenty more opposing the Camas runner's participation showed up Saturday. One of them was Jasmin Faulk, the executive director of Women's Liberation Front (WOLF) — who lost her job at a community college due to a blog post about how "biology still matters." Her emphasis? That fairness in sports shouldn't be a partisan issue. "The issue is really about the safety and the fairness for women and girls," Faulk said. "That's why we're here, that's why WOLF has chosen to participate and be vocal on this. We have fought for women's rights on all levels and in all areas and sports is just another one that is fairly agreed upon as a general view. This one's an easy one for us to stand by." I mentioned to her that this doesn’t really feel like a right/left issue — that most Democrats support the separation of biological males and females in sports. WASHINGTON HIGH SCHOOL GIRL WALKS OFF STARTING LINE ALONE IN PROTEST OF TRANS RUNNER, ENDING HER SEASON "It's unfortunate, though, because the Democrats are not voicing that. I think that's where the frustration is," Faulk said. "It's a lot easier for the right to take a stand on this one because they've kind of been consistent on this issue for a long time, but the Democrats, I think, have been quieted into it, and the fearmongering in the movement has been the hardest for a lot of people." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The fear is real. Despite this being an 80-20 issue, most people don't want their name attached to their opinions on this matter. One male cross-country runner came over to the crowd wearing XX-XY Athletics gear and said, "I like your shirts" — but said he couldn't accept a "save girls' sports" bracelet or comment on the subject. A female cross-country runner took a picture with that same crowd and said, "You can believe you are something, but you're affecting other people who are actually that and have worked really, really hard for this, and you're taking away a spot from a girl who trained all season." She approached me twice afterward to make sure I wouldn't use her name or school. But then there are people such as Dawn Land, who held up a sign Saturday reading "Girls deserve fair sports!" "I think that this boy that is running in the girls' race is grossly unfair. And I'm disgusted at the adults that allowed this to happen," Land said. Well, Tuesday, adults will have a chance to make sure this doesn't happen in Washington state again. On the ballot is Initiative 638, which would prohibit biological males from competing in girls' K-12 sports. articles.title: Fake claims, evasion of Rs 5.3 crore land, techie couple in I-T net
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In a stern message to those making false income tax claims, authorities have carried out a rare search action on an IT professional and his
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a stern message to those making false income tax claims, authorities have carried out a rare search action on an IT professional and his wife, estimating alleged bogus claims and tax evasion of Rs 5.3 crore over five years, according to the department. The couple also face charges of forging documents.Tax officials found that deduction claims involved fake political donations, interest on home and education loans, while rental income was not disclosed. They had purchased half-a-dozen properties using some of these funds.It all started with the wife's tax return claiming a deduction of over Rs 40 lakh for a donation to a political party. While her Form 16 showed deductions of around Rs 1.2 lakh, the return claimed an additional deduction. When the claim was verified with the party, officials found that the taxpayer had actually donated Rs 50, for which a receipt had been issued. Investigators found that the receipt had been digitally modified and several fabricated receipts generated to support the claim of a donation exceeding Rs 40 lakh.But the couple, who live in Delhi-NCR, did not give in easily. When summoned during the investigation, the husband, who filed the returns, not only presented the "modified" receipts but also submitted bank statements to support the claim. Officials sought to verify the statements with the bank, as the transactions did not tally.Loan payments, credit card payments and bank transfers, including transfers to their own account, had been forged to show them as political donations.The couple had claimed nearly Rs 3 crore in education loan interest for studies at Yale University. An interest certificate was submitted. During probe, officials discovered that no family member of the couple under scrutiny had ever studied at Yale and that the certificate had been prepared using ChatGPT.The couple also made a bogus housing loan claim, with both spouses describing themselves as the sole owner of the same property, although they have now admitted that it was jointly owned. Contrary to their claims, the property was always rented out and was not self-occupied.In their returns, one spouse had claimed nil rental income and interest payment of Rs 2 lakh, while the other had claimed up to Rs 5 lakh as interest income. Since tax returns now require individuals to disclose loan account number and the bank, the name of the bank was changed in one case and the loan amount increased to Rs 6 crore, with interest claimed at Rs 8 lakh. The probe revealed that the loan had been repaid in 2015, while the claims under scrutiny related to the period beginning FY2021-22. The property was earning rent of Rs 10-16 lakh during this period.Dealing with the couple has not been easy. When their case was first picked up, the husband shifted the deduction claim for political donations under Section 80GGC to donations to charities under Section 80G, without surrendering the claim.The couple now face penalties and other legal action.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US Army veteran and single mother receives donated Cadillac after struggling to transport her daughter with disabilities to appointments and activities
articles.summary: A US Army veteran and single mother from East Northport, New York, received a donated Cadillac XT5 after struggling with transportation while caring for
articles.body: A US Army veteran and single mother from East Northport, New York, received a donated Cadillac XT5 after struggling with transportation while caring for her daughter, Chloe, who has disabilities. Christina, who served in the US Army from 2004 to 2009, including a deployment to Iraq, was surprised with the vehicle through a community fundraising effort involving veterans' organisations, labour unions and local businesses. The donation aims to help the family manage everyday journeys, attend medical appointments and access educational and recreational activities. The initiative also received a $30,000 contribution from the Building & Construction Trades Council of Nassau & Suffolk Counties.Why did a US Army veteran and single mother need a donated CadillacReliable transportation had been one of the biggest challenges for Christina and her family. As a single mother caring for Chloe, who has disabilities and is homeschooled, she faced difficulties arranging regular journeys for essential errands and activities. Christina also lives with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), adding to the challenges she has experienced.The donated vehicle is expected to make everyday travel easier for the family. Speaking after receiving the keys, Christina explained how having her own transportation would change her daily routine. She said: "I get to go to the grocery store, drive myself to doctor's appointments. I'm so excited to just be able to be out there on the road and have my freedom again."How will the donated car help Chloe visit libraries and aquariumsThe vehicle is also expected to give Chloe greater access to educational and recreational opportunities. Since she is homeschooled, having reliable transportation will make it easier for her to visit places outside the home, including libraries and aquariums, without her mother having to arrange paid transport.Explaining the difference the donation would make, Christina said: "Now she gets to go to the aquarium, the library, whenever she wants without having to take Uber." She also described the gift as something that would significantly affect their family life, adding: "This is literally going to change our lives."How did local organisations help fund a donated Cadillac for a veteranThe donation was made possible through contributions from the McNamara Charity Golf Outing, King O'Rourke Cadillac, Suffolk County labour unions and veterans' organisations, including Paws of War and United Veterans Beacon House. The McNamara Charity Golf Outing, run by Chris McNamara, has been organising fundraising activities for veterans, their families and first responders for 17 years.McNamara explained that support from local trades and community organisations helped cover the cost of the Cadillac. This arrangement also meant that donations collected through the golf outing could be redirected towards other needs, including rent, medical expenses and insurance. He said: "We're giving back to veterans and first responders. So many people stepped up with us."How did a $30,000 contribution help a US Army veteran and her daughterState Senator Mario Mattera also acknowledged the role played by Suffolk County's labour community and veterans' organisations in making the donation possible. According to News 12 New York, the Building & Construction Trades Council of Nassau & Suffolk Counties (NSBCTC) contributed $30,000 towards purchasing the vehicle.Mattera praised the organisations and individuals who came together to support the veteran, describing the initiative as a way of recognising the service of military personnel. He said: "We are so proud that we are giving back to people who protected us from harm's way. It is not a handout - it's a hand up. We could never do enough for our veterans."For Christina, receiving the Cadillac was an unexpected moment. She said she had not known about the planned donation before the presentation and expressed her gratitude to everyone involved. "I had no idea that this was going to even happen," she said. "My heart is so full right now."The vehicle provides Christina with a way to manage her family's transportation needs while continuing to support other veterans facing difficulties. She described the donation as a fresh start, allowing her and Chloe to travel more independently and take part in activities that had previously been difficult to access.You use AI every day. articles.title: Initial results indicate victory for Iotova in Bulgarian presidential vote
articles.summary: Acting President Iotova would become nation’s first elected female head of state if official results confirm her win.
articles.body:
Acting President Iliana Iotova is the apparent winner of Bulgaria’s presidential run-off according to initial results, as her rival has conceded defeat.

Iotova, who advocates for dialogue with Russia and opposes military aid to Ukraine, received 58 percent of the vote in Sunday’s run-off , according to the count by several polling agencies.

If confirmed by official results, she would become Bulgaria’s first elected female head of state.

Her opponent, former interim Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov, is said to be trailing at about 38 percent.

Gyurov, who is backed by the pro-Western opposition, said the results had to be accepted as they stood.

“This is how the Bulgarian citizens have voted,” he said.

Exit polls put voter participation at about 27 to 29 percent, slightly higher ‌than the first-round race last week, which had a record-low turnout of 23 percent.

Official results are expected on Monday as ballots are counted for the presidency which is largely ceremonial.

61-year-old Iotova took over as acting president in January, when her longtime ally Prime Minister Rumen Radev resigned to run in, and win, a parliamentary election.

“I don’t like either of the two candidates,” Krassimira Kostova, a 64-year-old teacher in the capital Sofia, who voted anyway, told the AFP news agency.

Petar Doitchinov, a 67-year-old retired engineer, said he had skipped the first round last week because he expected a run-off. He said he voted for “the lesser evil”, as neither candidate matched his “vision of democracy”.

The vote comes as 21 people remain missing following a series of drone attacks last month on commercial vessels off the country’s Black Sea coast. They are suspected to be spillover from the Russia-Ukraine war.

PM Radev has said that the attacks appear to serve Russian interests and summoned the Russian ambassador, though his government said there was no evidence directly linking them to Moscow.

Both presidential candidates have condemned the attacks and called for a diplomatic end to the war in Ukraine.

Gyurov, a banker and former caretaker prime minister, criticised Iotova in a television debate for not explicitly blaming Russia. “Russia must stop its aggression so that the next steps can be taken,” he said.

Iotova said that “peace can come only through negotiations”. After voting, she said she wanted “Bulgaria to be strong in a strong Europe” and “sovereign in its decisions”.

In the first round of voting last week , Iotova won 35 percent, with Gyurov on 32 percent – a much narrower gap than the 20-point lead predicted by opinion polls for Iotova.

Political analyst Teodor Slavev told AFP that voters were passing judgement on “Iotova’s unconvincing response regarding Russian threats in the Black Sea”.

articles.title: Jet crashes in Florida, killing all 9 on board
articles.summary: All nine people on board a Learjet 60 jet died in a “cataclysmic” crash in Florida on Sunday afternoon, officials said.
articles.body: All nine people on board a Learjet 60 jet died in a “cataclysmic” crash in Florida on Sunday afternoon, officials said. The flight, which departed from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, crashed near Cresthaven around 12:50 p.m., the Federal Aviation Administration said. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said all nine on the flight died. He called the crash a “horrific tragedy” on social media, adding, “Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost.” The identities of the people on board have not been released. Video showed a crater in the middle of a road engulfed in flames. In distressing air traffic control audio, a woman can be heard saying, “Mayday, mayday. We’re descending 10,000 feet per minute.” She later frantically yells, saying the jet was descending at 20,000 feet per minute. “We’re gonna crash into the ground 722 Bravo Delta,” she can be heard saying, followed by a scream. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis described the crash as “cataclysmic.” “It looked like a missile going down. It left a big crater on the side of the road,” DeSantis told reporters after the crash. He said the crash spewed a large amount of debris that spanned a “pretty significant distance” but that there were no reports of anyone on the ground being injured or killed. The aircraft is registered to an LLC in Delaware, according to FAA records. The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating the crash. The Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office said an aircraft incident was under investigation in the area of Military Trail, and all northbound and southbound lanes are closed until further notice.

articles.title: Carney signals progress on Canada-US trade deal talks as midterms loom
articles.summary: Canadian PM Mark Carney announces progress in Canada-US trade deal talks ahead of Tuesday’s US midterm elections.
articles.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has announced progress towards a future trade deal with the United States, which could help ease tensions between the two North American neighbours.

The Sunday announcement came just two days before the November 3 US midterm elections, which will determine control of the US Congress.

“Good conversation with US President Donald Trump on the future of Canada-U.S. trade,” Carney posted on X on Sunday.

Ties between Ottawa and Washington have been strained by an escalating trade war , with Canada and the US imposing billions of dollars in tariffs on each other’s goods in recent months.

“Teams from both countries will be working in the coming weeks to deliver that outcome,” Carney said. “This builds on recent constructive discussions on the outlines of a mutually beneficial trade deal.”

In his second term, Trump has upended global trade by imposing tariffs on many of the US’s allies, including Canada – one of the US’s biggest trading partners.

In August, high-level trade talks between Ottawa and Washington broke down, and Trump imposed a 50 percent levy on $20bn of Canadian goods, or 5.5 percent of its exports. Canada responded with equivalent tariffs on US steel, dairy, appliances, farm equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics.

Trump said last week that he expected a new trade agreement with Canada to be reached “pretty soon”, but offered no details.

The trade tensions with Canada have become an issue in the midterm elections, particularly in Michigan and Maine, where Republican candidates have faced pressure over tariffs that have hurt local businesses.

Canada has sought to diversify its trade options and recently welcomed a European Union offer to become an “associate member”.

Carney praised the proposal’s ambition, describing his goal as a “unique alliance” rather than conventional EU membership.

articles.body: The first edition of the College Football Playoff rankings will be released on November 3, marking a point in the 2026 college football season when the AP Top 25 Poll takes a back seat, but that doesn't mean we're going to start ignoring the always-controversial poll. Someone has to keep tabs on the AP voters who can't possibly watch all these games and are forced to scramble and put together a list of the best 25 teams in the country. With just two matchups featuring ranked opponents on the Week 8 slate, nobody was expecting too many fireworks, but the one boom we did get out in Los Angeles courtesy of USC, voters made sure to overreact. On the other side of the country, Wake Forest moved to 7-1 and continued its run of absolutely throttling opponents, but apparently, outscoring your last two opponents 92-14 doesn't matter much. Week 9 AP Top 25 Poll Voters managed to put together the correct collection of the Top 5 teams in the country, but did so in the incorrect order. A shocking development, we know. While Miami played with its food in Chapel Hill on Saturday, the Hurricanes improved to 8-0 and are the most-talented and most-explosive of the three unbeaten teams remaining, making the No. 1 next to their name completely justified. THESE NUMBERS SHOW JUST HOW FRAUDULENT NOTRE DAME HAS BEEN DURING THE MARCUS FREEMAN ERA Georgia did exactly what was expected of it by throttling Florida following a bye week after its inexplicable loss at home to Auburn. articles.title: In the 12th century, Nepalese artisans made a 93cm gilt-copper Manjushri statue; after Geneva, New York and Asian collections, it sold for about Rs 166 crore in 2026, setting a Himalayan gilt-bronze auction record
articles.summary: From every curve to every carving, such is the intricacy of this 12th-century Manjushri sculpture from Nepal.
articles.body: From every curve to every carving, such is the intricacy of this 12th-century Manjushri sculpture from Nepal. Standing nearly a metre tall, this gilded copper figure of Manjushri, the Bodhisattva of Transcendent Wisdom, is a remarkable example of the artistic excellence of the Kathmandu Valley. Created by Newar artisans at a time when Nepal was emerging as one of the most important centres of Buddhist art, the sculpture has travelled across continents and collections over the centuries. Now in 2026, it is making headlines once again, selling for approximately ₹166 crore at auction and setting a record for Himalayan gilt-bronze art.But what makes this sculpture worth such an extraordinary sum is not just its age, size or the gold that covers its surface. It is a rare surviving example of a sculptural tradition that helped shape Buddhist art across the Himalayas and beyond.The artistry of Newar craftsmanshipThe 93cm sculpture depicts Manjushri, a bodhisattva associated with wisdom and enlightenment in Buddhist tradition. He is identified by the Prajnaparamita Sutra, the Buddhist scripture representing transcendent wisdom, placed upon a flowering lotus at his shoulder. The figure is dressed in elaborate jewellery, including necklaces, armlets, bracelets and a sacred thread, all carefully detailed against the smooth, gilded copper surface.Look closely at the sculpture's remarkable proportions: the elongated body, slender waist, gently curved hips and flowing silhouette give it an almost weightless appearance, despite its imposing size. The complex 3 bend pose, called tribhanga, creates an impression of movement, rendering the figure less an inanimate object and more a living form, moving like poetry in front of us. Its gilt surface used to shimmer in the flickering light of temple lamps, giving the bodhisattva an almost ethereal quality.These characteristics are the hallmark of the Newar school of sculpture, a tradition that was built by the Newar artisans of the Kathmandu Valley of Nepal. These craftsmen are revered as some of the best metalworkers of the Buddhist world from the 9-12th centuries. They were also adept at the subtle art of mercury gilding, which gave the sculptures their brilliant golden finish.What set Newar craftsmanship apart, however, was its ability to fuse the classical ideals of Indian art with a distinctly Nepalese sense of proportion, ornamentation and form. Their sculptures often showed Buddhist deities as young princely figures, adorned with elaborate jewellery but with a clear spiritual presence. Of course, the Manjushri showcases their craftsmanship beautifully.How Nepalese artisans influenced Buddhist art across AsiaThe importance of Newar craftsmanship is not just limited to Nepal. Geographically positioned between the Buddhist centres of northern India and Tibet, the Kathmandu Valley became an important centre for preserving and developing Buddhist artistic traditions.Between the 10th and 12th centuries, Tibet experienced a renewed expansion of Buddhist institutions, a period known as the Later Diffusion of Buddhism. The construction and restoration of monasteries created a growing demand for sacred sculptures, and Nepalese artisans were particularly well placed to fulfil it. Their ability to produce monumental gilt-copper figures made their work highly sought after by Tibetan patrons.But this exchange was not just about completed sculptures moving across the Himalayas. Newar craftsmen also went to Tibet, teaching local artists their skills in metal casting, gilding and sculptural proportions. These techniques were eventually incorporated into Tibetan art, creating a shared visual language strongly influenced by Nepalese aesthetics.The influence eventually reached the imperial courts of China. Anige, a celebrated Nepalese artist, in fact, worked under the patronage of the Yuan dynasty in the 13th century. He and the artists associated with him helped establish a Himalayan-inspired style of Buddhist art at the Mongol court. Its influence continued through the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties, particularly in the proportions, jewellery and refined modelling of sculptures made for Tibetan Buddhist patrons.A rare sculpture with an extraordinary historyThe Manjushri's importance is also reflected in the relatively small number of comparable sculptures that have survived. Some Nepalese-style monumental bodhisattvas remain in important Tibetan religious institutions, including Sera Monastery, the Potala Palace, Jokhang Temple and Shalu Monastery. Others are preserved in international museums, including the British Museum, the Victoria and Albert Museum and the Norton Simon Museum of Art in California.Sculptures of this age and scale are particularly rare. While smaller Nepalese gilt-copper figures can be found in museum collections and monastery treasuries, few retain the combination of monumental proportions, intricate detailing and exceptional craftsmanship seen in this Manjushri.Its own history is equally interesting. According to Christie's, the sculpture belonged to the George Ortiz Collection in Geneva by 2002, before passing through an important private collection in New York and the Asian art dealership Carlton Rochell Asian Art in 2017. It later entered a private Asian collection. It was also exhibited at the Art Institute of Chicago in 2003 and at the Zhiguan Museum of Fine Art in Beijing in 2018, bringing the centuries-old work before international audiences.On 30 October 2026, the sculpture went under the hammer at Christie's Hong Kong as part of Awakening Wisdom: Masterpieces of Buddhist Art from a Private Asian Collection. It sold for HK$137.35 million, approximately Rs 166 crore, setting a world auction record for a Himalayan gilt-bronze sculpture.The Manjushri is a reminder of the artistic legacy of the Kathmandu Valley beyond its extraordinary auction price. It was produced nearly 9 centuries ago, an era when Nepalese artists contributed to the visual vocabulary of Buddhist art in Tibet and China. Much more than an expensive antiquity, its survival, remarkable craftsmanship and journey through international collections make it much more than an expensive antiquity. It is a piece of Nepal's artistic history, one that continues to illuminate the influence of Newar craftsmen on the wider Buddhist world.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Dakota Johnson sells her 1947 Carl Maston-designed Los Angeles home for $5.92 million, nearly $2.4 million more than she paid in 2016, after it went contingent in nine days
articles.summary: Dakota Johnson’s midcentury home at 1657 Marmont Avenue in Los Angeles sold for approximately $5.92 million on June 29, 2026, according to its MLS history
articles.body: Dakota Johnson’s midcentury home at 1657 Marmont Avenue in Los Angeles sold for approximately $5.92 million on June 29, 2026, according to its MLS history on Redfin. The property was listed on May 25 for $6 million and marked contingent on June 3, nine days later. Built in 1947 by architect Carl Maston, the 3,210-square-foot house has three bedrooms and three bathrooms. It sits above the Chateau Marmont, close to the Sunset Strip, and became widely known after Johnson featured it in an Architectural Digest home tour in 2020. She bought the property in January 2016 for $3.55 million, a difference of about $2.37 million between the reported purchase and sale prices before transaction costs and other expenses.Dakota Johnson’s Los Angeles home sells for $5.92 million after going contingent in nine daysThe property’s MLS history records a May 25, 2026, listing date and an asking price of $6 million. It was marked contingent on June 3, nine days after it entered the market, and sold on June 29 for $5,924,372. Redfin also displays a public-record sale figure of $5,924,500. The Real Deal reported a slightly different asking price of $5.95 million, but the MLS history records the original listing at $6 million. The home was listed by Ruby Fay of Engel & Völkers Beverly Hills. The buyer’s identity has not been disclosed in the reports reviewed. The address is in Los Angeles County, in the Hollywood Hills West area. Some coverage has described the property as being in West Hollywood, but Redfin identifies the municipality as Los Angeles.Inside Dakota Johnson’s 1947 Carl Maston-designed midcentury homeMaston designed the house in 1947. In her 2020 Architectural Digest home tour, Johnson described him as a friend of modernist architects Richard Neutra and John Lautner. She explained that the architects would meet at Musso & Frank’s because they were all in love with a hostess at the restaurant. Maston later married her, and, as Johnson explained, the house was where the couple lived. Johnson bought the property in January 2016 for $3.55 million, using her first major Fifty Shades paycheck. She later worked with design firm Pierce & Ward on its interiors, retaining features such as exposed beams, wood panelling, brickwork and expansive glass walls. The design connects the living spaces to the outdoor area, where large windows open toward the swimming pool.The home’s kitchen became widely recognised after Johnson’s Architectural Digest video tour circulated online in 2020. In a January 2021 appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Johnson explained that the bowl of limes on the counter had been set dressing and that she had played along during the tour. In the same interview, she said she was mildly allergic to limes. The allergy admission added another layer to the already viral kitchen moment. Architectural Digest reported that the primary bathroom’s cabinets were painted a dusty-rose shade to match a sweater Johnson owned from The Row. The room includes a soaking tub and double sinks. Outside, the property has a swimming pool, terraces, a fire pit and mature landscaping. Its glass walls and outdoor spaces were among the features highlighted in the Architectural Digest tour.Dakota Johnson buys another Los Angeles home in Outpost EstatesIn October 2025, Johnson purchased another Los Angeles property in the Outpost Estates neighbourhood for about $5.3 million, according to The Star. The Mediterranean-style home was reported to have approximately 3,550 square feet of living space, with three bedrooms and three-and-a-half bathrooms, as well as a separate guest apartment with one bedroom and one bathroom. The Marmont Avenue property’s reported sale price was about $2.37 million higher than Johnson’s 2016 purchase price. That difference does not account for renovation expenses, taxes, fees or other costs associated with owning and selling the home.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Kherson braces for return of war as localised Russia-Ukraine truce ends
articles.summary: Moscow and Kyiv continue strikes elsewhere, but no reported violations in Kherson region during the six-day ceasefire.
articles.body:
The longest multi-day truce between Russia and Ukraine, limited to Ukraine’s eastern Kherson region, has come to an end with no violations reported by either side, but also no sign of an extension.

The truce, which ended on Sunday night, allowed hundreds of besieged residents of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky to be evacuated in a rare joint operation between Kyiv and Moscow.

Russian strikes elsewhere in Ukraine on Sunday left hundreds of thousands of households without power, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. In Russia, meanwhile, authorities reported major ⁠damage to an industrial site following Ukrainian drone attacks on the Nizhny Novgorod region.

The six-day localised ceasefire in the front-line Oleshky and the surrounding area was reached after mediation efforts by United States First Lady Melania Trump and with the involvement of Pope Leo XIV. It was set to expire at 10:59pm Ukraine time (20:59 GMT).

On Sunday, Ukraine’s military said it evacuated 167 more people from threatened areas of the southern Kherson region, including 22 children and 21 people with limited mobility requiring special assistance.

“Units of civil-military cooperation of the ‘South’ group of forces, in cooperation with representatives of local authorities, evacuated 167 civilians to safer points in the Kherson region,” Ukraine’s General Staff wrote on Telegram.

An estimated 2,000 civilians were in Oleshky when the temporary truce took hold. They were offered the choice to evacuate to Kyiv-controlled territory of Ukraine or territory occupied by Russia, or to remain in the city with replenished food and medical supplies.

“The ceasefire across Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region has provided residents with the freedom to move, access to food, clean water, medicine, plus a renewed sense of dignity without the constant threat of attack,” Melania Trump said on social media. “Let Oleshky become the starting point for lasting peace.”

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, quoted by Russian news agencies, said Moscow had a positive view of how the operation was conducted in Oleshky, as well as of the coordination between the two countries’ human rights commissioners.

A Ukrainian official, however, told the AFP news agency that Russia reportedly refused an offer to extend the ceasefire after Kyiv’s Foreign Ministry proposed it.

Since Russia launched a full-scale invasion of its neighbour in February 2022, Moscow’s forces have occupied most of the eastern Ukrainian regions of Donetsk and Luhansk, as well as the majority of territory in Ukraine’s southern Kherson and Zaporizhia regions.

Kherson Governor Oleksandr Prokudin urged residents to be vigilant as the expiry of the ceasefire neared on Sunday.

“I also strongly urge you not to visit the so-called ‘red zones’ – areas and settlements near the Dnipro [River],” Prokudin wrote on Telegram. “The intensity of Russian strikes there remains high, and the threat to life is extremely high.”

Residents in Kherson city, one of the remaining areas of the region still controlled by Ukraine, remained calm, despite knowing the quiet of the localised ceasefire would soon end.

“Don’t be afraid, keep holding on,” Oleksandr Knyha, head of the Mykola Kulish Kherson Regional Academic Music and Drama Theater, told the audience as he opened a concert.

Knyha is from Oleshky and used to commute from there to Kherson for work. He has not given up hope of returning home.

“That’s also what keeps me here,” he told the Associated Press news agency.

Elsewhere, Moscow and Kyiv have continued air strikes, with Zelenskyy saying on Sunday that Russia continues to target Ukraine’s energy systems before winter. Attacks on power infrastructure in four Ukrainian regions overnight cut electricity to hundreds of thousands of households, he said.

A Russian attack also killed three people, including a 13-year-old girl, in the Ukrainian region of Vinnytsia, when a drone hit the grounds of a vocational school, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said. Four others were wounded.

Russian drone attacks targeting Ukraine’s Kyiv region for a second consecutive day wounded a woman and damaged homes, energy infrastructure and a retail establishment, regional authorities said.

In its daily report on Sunday, Ukraine’s Air Force said that Moscow’s forces attacked Ukraine with 433 drones overnight, of which 371 were destroyed or suppressed.

Meanwhile, more than 100 Ukrainian drones were shot down over the skies of Russia’s Nizhny Novgorod region east of Moscow, Governor Gleb Nikitin said on Sunday.

The attack sparked a blaze at the Kstovo oil refinery, Russian media outlets reported, sharing images of black plumes of smoke over the horizon.

Zelenskyy said Kyiv also struck a factory for missile components and air defence facilities in Russia’s southern Rostov region.

“We are justly defending ourselves against Russian aggression and doing everything to reduce Russia’s capability to continue it,” Zelenskyy said.

articles.title: Ukraine air raid app apparently hacked as users receive false radiation alert, Air Force says
articles.summary: Authorities say there is no threat and have advised the public to stay calm and follow official channels for information.
articles.body:
Ukraine's air raid alert app was apparently hacked on Sunday and for a short time said the capital Kyiv was subject to a radiation threat, the Ukrainian Air Force has said.

The Air Force message on Telegram read: "The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel."

The Ukrainian Central Intelligence Agency said on Telegram that there had been a failure in the app, and urged people to use other sources of information to clarify the situation regarding the threat of air strikes.

The messages, in Ukrainian, started at approximately 22:47 (20:47 GMT), with the first reading: "Radiation threat. Radiation threat declared in Kyiv."

The next alert, written in Russian, came at 22:48, which read: "Hi! There will be a nuclear alert across Ukraine. Don't worry, it's Oreshnik flying".

A third alert, at 22:49, again in Ukrainian, said "Chemical threat. There is a threat of a chemical attack on Kyiv. Don't go outside."

At 22:49, a fourth alert stated there was a "Street fighting threat. Street fighting is taking place in Kyiv. Don't go outside."

A series of all clear messages were then delivered to users' phones, which were connected to each of the previous alerts, individually declaring each threat clear.

In a separate post, the Ukrainian Central Intelligence Agency said that due to the Air Alert application, the Radiation Hazard signal was played on loudspeaker devices in the Lviv region, and added there was no threat of radiation hazard.

It advised the public to turn on notifications on your smartphone, pay attention to sirens, and to only read official sources.

The governor of Vinnytsia oblast, Natalya Zabolotna said there had been a cyberattack on the Air Alert app and posted a warning on Telegram not to click on the link in the message.

The Air Alert app is supported by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, and informs users instantly about the beginning and end of defence alerts.

articles.title: Meet California twins Henry and Jack Grover, whose sprayable hydrogel kept hot charcoal from reigniting for 27 minutes, nine times longer than water in their test
articles.summary: Twin brothers from Riverside, California, have developed a sprayable hydrogel designed to help prevent wildfires from reigniting.
articles.body: Twin brothers from Riverside, California, have developed a sprayable hydrogel designed to help prevent wildfires from reigniting. Henry Grover and his twin brother Jack began the project after learning that the 2025 Palisades fire had been started by an earlier blaze that reignited. Their work focused on whether a hydrogel could be applied to burned areas and help stop them from catching fire again.The twins' final gel hydrated in 15 minutes and prevented charcoal briquettes from relighting for 27 minutes, according to the Society for Science. They also developed a sprayer capable of projecting the gel up to 18.3 metres. Their project was titled “Sprayable Hydrogels for Preventing the Rekindling of Wildfires” and was featured among the 2026 Junior Innovators Challenge finalists.What inspired the twins to develop a fire-prevention hydrogelThe project was inspired by the 2025 Palisades fire in California. Henry and Jack realised that firefighters could struggle to apply enough water to burned areas to stop them from reigniting.They began exploring whether hydrogel could help solve this problem. Henry said, “We knew that hydrogel was capable of absorbing hundreds of times its weight in water and releasing it over a short period of time, so we wanted to use it to prevent rekindling.”How the twins tested different hydrogels to find the best materialThe twins began by soaking nine hydrogels in water and weighing them. They then dried the samples in an oven and measured them at 15-minute intervals. Next, they tested how well each material adhered to surfaces. They spread the hydrogels on leaves, hung the leaves vertically, and measured how much of the gel’s weight was lost from each leaf.These tests helped them narrow the options to two hydrogels. The brothers then compared how quickly the remaining materials hydrated. They soaked both in water and weighed them for up to three hours.The final hydrogel kept hot charcoal from relighting for 27 minutesThe twins selected sodium polyacrylate as their preferred material. It hydrated in 15 minutes. They applied the gel to hot charcoal briquettes and measured how long the charcoal took to reignite. In their test, briquettes sprayed with water relit after three minutes. Those treated with the hydrogel took 27 minutes to relight.The result showed a longer delay in reignition under the conditions of their experiment. Henry and Jack also designed a sprayer for applying the gel. The device was able to spray the material 18.3 metres. The Society for Science featured the work under the project title “Sprayable Hydrogels for Preventing the Rekindling of Wildfires”.From restoring a vintage robot to animating his own screenplayBeyond the wildfire project, Henry has worked on restoring a robot from the 1980s. He updated it so that it could work with modern technology. Henry said, “The change was nothing short of magical. articles.title: High-ranking US Democratic senator suffers stroke
articles.summary: Senator Chris Murphy, a fierce Trump critic who is not up for re-election in the midterms, is ‘alert’ after a stroke.
articles.body:
United States Senator Chris Murphy , a high-ranking Democratic legislator, has suffered a stroke but is “awake and alert”, his senior aide said.

Murphy remained hospitalised on Sunday after seeking medical care for numbness in his arm the day before, his chief-of-staff, Allison Herwitt, said in a statement.

She said he was “responding well to treatment” at John Hopkins, one of the country’s top hospitals.

“The doctors are encouraged by his progress, he is awake and alert, and we are optimistic he will make a full recovery,” Herwitt said.

Murphy is not up for re-election in Tuesday’s midterms that will decide which party controls Congress, but is considered a potential presidential candidate in 2028.

A 20-year senator from the state of Connecticut, Murphy serves as a top Democrat on two powerful Senate committees: appropriations, which decides how US government funds are allocated, and foreign relations.

Murphy toured the Middle East in October, the first regional trip by a US Democrat since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February.

He has been a fierce critic of US President Donald Trump and the Iran war, pledging that Democrats will withhold funding for the war if they win the Senate on Tuesday.

He accused the US Defense Department of denying him access to a US military base in Qatar during his trip last month and has pledged to investigate Trump and his family for alleged corruption if Democrats win the Senate.

Trump said he was “really surprised” to learn about Murphy’s stroke, adding that “nobody wants to have that”.

articles.title: Savannah Guthrie makes heartbreaking plea in mom's disappearance after finding old drawing
articles.summary: Savannah Guthrie shared her daughter's emotional drawing in a new plea for answers nine months after Nancy Guthrie vanished from her Tucson home.
articles.body: "TODAY" co-host Savannah Guthrie issued a new plea for information about her missing mother, Nancy Guthrie, on Sunday, nine months after the 84-year-old was abducted from her Tucson, Arizona, home. Guthrie shared an old drawing made by her daughter, Vale, showing a blue umbrella in the rain and the words, "I know it might not seem like it, but I really need my mommy." "Found this old drawing from my daughter today," Guthrie wrote on Instagram. "It says so much about how I feel." "The world goes on, things appear ‘normal’ — as we try to keep going and be strong, especially for our young kids — but it’s not and it never will be," she continued. SAVANNAH GUTHRIE URGES PUBLIC TO HELP FIND MISSING MOTHER NANCY IN EMOTIONAL MOTHER’S DAY POST "For Annie and Tommy, for Cam and Kristine, for Mike and me and for all of Mom’s beloved grandchildren: We ache for her, we cry out for answers, we cannot move forward," Guthrie wrote. "We need someone to help us, tell us what you know. Our mom was a light in this world. We want to celebrate her and give her the dignity she deserves. The reward is still available. Please. We are begging you. Please help us." Guthrie also thanked those who have supported her family and urged people to "join us in praying without ceasing." THREE MONTHS AFTER NANCY GUTHRIE'S ABDUCTION, SHERIFF'S OFFICE RENEWS PLEA AS KEY QUESTIONS REMAIN UNANSWERED Nancy Guthrie was reported missing Feb. 1 after she was last seen at her home in the Catalina Foothills area near Tucson shortly before 10 p.m. Jan. 31. Authorities believe she was taken against her will. A masked, armed individual was captured on the home's doorbell camera footage, apparently tampering with the device. The FBI and Pima County Sheriff’s Department have not identified a suspect, and no arrests have been made. SAVANNAH GUTHRIE WAS 'SURPRISED AND DISMAYED' BY DOUBTS SHE WOULD RETURN TO 'TODAY' AFTER MOM'S DISAPPEARANCE Guthrie has continued to push for answers about her mother’s disappearance while returning to work on "TODAY." During a June appearance on "TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle," she rejected the idea that she had forgotten about her mother. "I know maybe people wonder, ‘What’s going on? How is she able to do that job? Is she not thinking about it? Did she forget?’ No. Never," Guthrie said. "It’s always with me. I cry every morning on the way to work, and I cry every morning on the way home," she added. SAVANNAH GUTHRIE DELIVERS 'VERY SPECIFIC' MESSAGE TO MOM'S KIDNAPPER 25 WEEKS AFTER HER ABDUCTION In August, six months after her mother's disappearance, Guthrie and her siblings also issued a statement asking for information about their mother. "Every day, we wake up and try to be strong and go on — because that’s what our joyful and resilient Mom taught us to do. But make no mistake — our hearts are in ruins," Guthrie wrote. "Cam and Kristine, Annie and Tommy, Mike and me — we spend every waking moment thinking of her, longing for her, looking for her." The Pima County Sheriff’s Department said Friday the Nancy Guthrie Task Force was continuing to work with laboratories to advance DNA analysis. "Earlier this month, investigators traveled to Florida to meet with lab scientists to see what more could be done to advance this case," the department wrote on X. "A number of ideas were discussed, and we continue to work with all our partners to solve this case." The agency reminded the public that no tip is too small. Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos previously said Guthrie "did not leave on her own." NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM DEMANDS RELEASED BY PIMA COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT IN BID TO IDENTIFY SENDER Authorities released the contents of two ransom notes in July. The first, sent Feb. 2, claimed Guthrie was safe and demanded $4 million in bitcoin for her release. The second, sent four days later, claimed she had died shortly after being kidnapped. Investigators said the notes contained distinctive writing patterns and asked anyone who recognized the style to contact authorities. A possible additional ransom text message reported in September was later deemed not credible by investigators. articles.summary: Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., endorsed Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers on Sunday, a major shake-up in the final stages of a top battleground race that could determine which party controls the Senate.
articles.body: Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., endorsed Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers on Sunday, a major shake-up in the final stages of a top battleground race that could determine which party controls the Senate. The congresswoman’s announcement marks a whirlwind turnabout from just days ago, amid a dispute with Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed’s campaign over an outside ad that Stevens said was antisemitic. NBC News reported Saturday that El-Sayed’s campaign had asked Stevens to no longer attend campaign events. “Hey, Michigan, as you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said that I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away,” Stevens said in a video. “And he’s right, and that’s why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today,” she said. Poll: Voters demand change and a check on Trump, fueling steep Democratic advantage Democrats have a sizable advantage in the battle for control of Congress days ahead of the midterm elections, a new national NBC News poll finds, with voters clamoring for change and voicing all-time high disapproval of President Donald Trump. Registered voters prefer a Democratic-controlled Congress by a 7-point margin, with Democrats leading Republicans 52%-45% — 2 points more than in last month’s poll. That includes a 21-point lead among independents. The president’s disapproval rating has climbed to 60%, a new high mark across his two terms in the NBC News poll. And for the first time in 30 years of NBC News polling, more voters say they are dissatisfied with their financial situation (51%) than satisfied (49%). But it’s not all good news for Democrats: The poll contains fresh signs that a number of voters are pushing back on the GOP, as opposed to falling in love with the Democratic Party. Federal judge dismisses Trump attempt to interfere in Alaska Senate race A federal judge in Alaska on Sunday dismissed the Trump administration’s lawsuit seeking to separate and preserve certain ballots in the state’s upcoming Senate election, where GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan faces Democrat Mary Peltola. In the last week, Peltola’s campaign has faced scrutiny after The New York Times reported the campaign and other Democrats recruited a candidate — Dan J. Sullivan — to run for the Senate with the same name as the incumbent senator. Citing potential voter confusion, the Trump administration sought to separate and preserve ballots with votes for Dan J. Sullivan, arguing that if the incumbent loses, it may be because people voted for the other Sullivan by mistake. In her ruling, U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason voiced concerns about voters’ right to a secret ballot. Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., declined to say whether he would accept the results of the Alaska Senate race if Peltola wins. Asked on NBC News’ “Meet the Press” whether he would accept the results if Peltola is certified to have won the Senate seat, Scott did not directly answer the question. “Dan Sullivan is going to win, Kristen,” he told moderator Kristen Welker. “You know that, and that’s the only thing I’m going to tell you, because it’s the truth.” Politics in brief Murphy hospitalized: Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., was hospitalized Saturday for a stroke after he “started experiencing numbness in his arm while at his son’s hockey game,” his chief of staff said in a statement. Called out: Democratic candidates in battleground races are throwing Joe Biden under the bus on the border.Signed, sealed, delivered: A federal judge tossed a revised version of Trump’s $10 billion defamation suit against The Wall Street Journal over a story about a birthday card he allegedly sent Jeffrey Epstein.Construction concerns: Virginia and the District of Columbia filed a lawsuit in a last-ditch effort to stop the construction of Trump’s planned triumphal arch. Stores looted in German riots as Gen Z activists protest living costs, military service Rioters looted stores and set fire to barricades in Frankfurt on Saturday as demonstrations across Germany called for lower living costs and better education. Tens of thousands of people took to the streets in more than 30 cities, including Berlin and Frankfurt, in protests organized by the campaign group Gen Z Regelt, or Gen Z Takes Charge. France, Italy, Serbia and Spain have seen protests against the cost of living, among other causes. As the demonstrations began Saturday afternoon in Paris, protesters were pictured holding a banner that read: “We do not need tear gas for our future to be blurry.” Martha Stewart responds to backlash over ‘hungry’ homeless Halloween costume Martha Stewart on Sunday responded to backlash about her Halloween costume, saying she was “distressed” to learn that her outfit, which depicted a “hungry” homeless person, had caused offense. Stewart shared a photo of herself in tattered clothing, holding a clipboard that read, “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!” She posed with a tired expression and makeup meant to look like dirt on her face. The photo was the third slide in an Instagram carousel promoting her candle collection on QVC. Many interpreted the costume as mocking the poor, and some called it “out of touch” and “dystopian.” Golden State Valkyries defeat Atlanta Dream for first WNBA title In only their second season in existence, the Golden State Valkyries are WNBA champions. The Valkyries won their first title on Saturday, defeating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history. Forward Gabby Williams led with 30 points and was named MVP. Williams scored just two points in the first half, but rallied with 28 in the second, a record for the most points scored in a half in the WNBA postseason. Teammate Kiah Stokes led rebounds at 13. “This is just incredible,” Stokes said of her fourth championship title. “But just my teammates, they’re amazing. The love that we feel is just incredible. I mean, this one just might be as good as my first.” Notable quote Extreme heat and drought, intensified by a “super” El Niño weather pattern, have made this Indonesia’s worst fire season in more than a decade. The persistent haze has affected millions across the region since the fires began in July, forcing school closures in several countries and fueling disputes over who is to blame. Protesters in Indonesia have accused their government of failing to act, while neighboring countries are threatening legal action. It was not immediately clear if there were additional injuries on the ground.Kimi Antonelli made Formula One history, becoming the youngest ever world champion at 20 years old after finishing third in the Mexico Grand Prix.A manhunt is underway for a shooter who killed one person and injured six in a Spirit Halloween store in what police in Fairfield, California, believe was a targeted incident. articles.title: UN warns of security risks in Western Sahara as peacekeeping mission ends
articles.summary: The mission, known as MINURSO, has been in place in the disputed region since a ceasefire in 1991.
articles.body:
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has warned of potential escalation of hostilities in the disputed Western Sahara region after the expiry of a 35-year-long peacekeeping mission .

“The Secretary-General said he remains concerned about the security situation throughout the territory and the risk of hostilities escalating,” his spokesperson, Stephane Dujarric, said in a statement on Sunday.

Guterres also confirmed the end of the peacekeeping mission on Sunday, after the UN Security Council (UNSC) failed to renew its mandate on Friday.

He urged all concerned “to exercise maximum restraint and to refrain from actions that could further increase tensions or undermine regional stability”.

November 1 marked the start of the “liquidation phase” of the peacekeeping mission, with assets transported back to troop-contributing countries, Guterres said.

The UN established the Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) in 1991 to monitor a ceasefire and prepare a referendum on the territory’s future.

Morocco has considered Western Sahara its territory since 1975, when Spain withdrew from the desert region in northwest Africa, roughly the size of Britain.

The Polisario Front, an Algeria-backed movement acting on behalf of the Indigenous Sahrawi people, seeks to establish an independent state called the Sahrawi Republic.

At the UNSC on Friday, the US proposed a resolution to support the principle of self-determination in the Western Sahara. Washington’s draft would have extended the mission for a year, removed “referendum” from its name and made Morocco’s autonomy proposal the only basis for further talks.

Russia vetoed the resolution, despite support from 11 of the 15 UNSC members, including fellow permanent members France and the United Kingdom.

The council then defeated a competing Russian resolution, leaving the mission to expire without a new mandate.

“While MINURSO’s peacekeeping operations have concluded, the United Nations stands ready to continue supporting efforts to advance dialogue and pursue a peaceful resolution of the conflict,” Guterres said on Sunday.

Morocco’s royal palace said the fact the mission was not renewed was a “significant development” in withdrawing the Western Sahara issue from the UNSC’s consideration.

On Saturday, Algeria’s Foreign Ministry, however, expressed “deep regret” over the non-renewal, blaming the “excessive bias” of the US towards Morocco’s position.

The Polisario Front said in a statement that it was “concerned at the deadlock in the Security Council meeting”.

Speaking after Friday’s vote, US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said it was truly unfortunate that in 2026, the veto was used to “preserve the letter R [in the Mission’s name] for referendum”.

He added Washington’s proposal “would have moved the 50-year conflict forward” and that the status quo is unacceptable.

Russia’s UN ambassador, Vassily Nebenzia, said at the same meeting that Moscow opposed the draft because it favoured one side.

“We stress the fact that the Security Council cannot automatically predetermine matters relating to sovereignty,” he said.

articles.title: New Buy Now Pay Later rules - don't get caught out
articles.summary: New affordability checks mean you could be blocked from using Buy Now Pay Later but here are ways to avoid it.
articles.body:
If you've bought something via Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) since the summer, then you'll have been tested to see if you can afford it.

BNPL has always been a type of loan, usually paid back in instalments, but it's only been officially regulated since July.

This means stricter background checks on your ability to repay.

If you fail, then your purchase via BNPL will be blocked. If there's a chance of this happening to you, here are some ways to approach the situation.

BNPL lenders - such as Klarna, Clearpay and others - must now have regulator approval to operate, giving shoppers more access to refunds and independent rulings on complaints if things go wrong.

But new affordability checks on each BNPL transaction could also leave you blocked from services for the first time.

There are different affordability checks for different purchases, partially based on how much is borrowed.

But, with the expensive festive season approaching, here's how to avoid being blocked when time and finances are tight.

Here are four things to consider if you find your account is closed or your borrowing limit has been massively reduced, from Sara Williams, a former volunteer debt adviser at Citizens Advice who posts tips as Debt Camel on social media.

Slow down your purchases: is what you are buying essential or can you postpone it?

Be more careful about what you buy to avoid needing a high credit limit to, for example, buy lots of clothes in different sizes

to escape the trap of having to use BNPL to make up for the cost of previous payments

Talk to debt charities for help and access to food bank vouchers if you are using BNPL for essentials

If you are struggling to make repayments on any type of loan - BNPL or otherwise - you should seek help before things spiral out of control.

The government-backed, independent, MoneyHelper website has a guide to finding free debt advice near you .

It also suggests writing down exactly what you owe, to help plan how you will repay the money.

There are also tools to work out if you are receiving all the benefits and grants you are entitled to, and a bill prioritiser to show which payments to make first and what to do if you miss a payment.

You should also be sceptical of supposed debt solutions you might see on your social feeds.
